platform_notes: All of these devices run Clover's own Android-based point-of-sale software (Clover apps such as Register, Sale, Printers, Setup, Diagnostics and the Kitchen Display and Kiosk apps), activated against the merchant's Clover account with an 8-digit activation code and managed from the Clover web dashboard; Clover Go is a Bluetooth card reader driven by the Clover Go app on the merchant's own phone or tablet. Sources are Clover's own help centre (including device-specific and "Hardware troubleshooting" articles that only appear to logged-in merchants but load by direct URL) and Clover quick start guides. Clover's articles tell merchants to "contact Clover support"; entries escalate those cases to our tech support.

entries.title: Blank or black screen, will not power on, or not responding: first checks
steps: Check that the device is plugged into a power source and every cable is firmly connected.
Restart the device, or do a hard reboot by holding the power button down for 10 seconds.
Check that the device is on a strong, stable Wi-Fi network, and restart your router if needed.
Swipe down from the top of the screen to open Settings and install a software update if one is offered.
Look for visible damage and re-seat any detachable part such as the printer or card reader.
If none of this helps, the device may need to be replaced.
entries.quote: If needed, restart your device or perform a hard reboot on your equipment by holding down the power button for 10 seconds.

entries.title: Check for a software update when a device misbehaves
steps: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the device Settings menu.
Update the software if the device prompts you to.
entries.quote: Open the device Settings menu by swiping down from the top of the screen, and update the software if prompted.

entries.title: Check a faulty device for damage and loose parts
steps: Look over the hardware for visible damage.
Take out and put back any detachable part, such as the printer or card reader.
Replace any lost or damaged cables or hubs.
entries.quote: Inspect the hardware for visible damage and reinsert any detachable components, such as the printer or card reader.

entries.title: Troubleshooting did not fix the device
steps: If the basic checks (power, reboot, network, updates, re-seating parts) do not fix it, the device may need to be replaced.
Contact support to arrange a replacement.
entries.quote: If troubleshooting steps do not resolve the issue, you may need to replace your device.

entries.title: How fast the internet needs to be for Clover
steps: Run a speed test at speedtest.net.
Clover recommends at least 8 Mbps download and 384 Kbps upload.
entries.quote: We recommend a minimum download speed of 8Mbps and an upload speed of 384Kbps

entries.title: Ways a Clover device can connect to the internet
steps: Depending on the device, it can connect by Ethernet, by Wi-Fi, or by the SIM card in the device over a cellular network.
entries.quote: you'll have the option to connect using Ethernet, WiFi, or the SIM card in the device, which can connect to a cellular network

entries.title: Use Ethernet for countertop devices and kitchen printers
steps: Connect countertop devices by Ethernet where you can; it is the most stable connection.
Put a kitchen printer on the same network as the other devices, or it cannot talk to them.
If you use Wi-Fi instead, make sure the kitchen printer is on the same Wi-Fi network as the other devices.
entries.quote: If you use WiFi, you must make sure the kitchen printer is on the same network as other devices.

entries.title: Wi-Fi requirements for Clover devices
steps: The router must be password-protected.
It must use at least WPA security; most modern routers default to WPA2.
entries.quote: Your router must be password-protected and have a minimum security level of WPA.

entries.title: Add or forget a Wi-Fi network after setup
steps: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the device settings.
Add the new Wi-Fi network or forget the old one there.
entries.quote: If you wish to add or forget a WiFi network after setting up, you may access the device settings by swiping down from the top of the screen at any time.

entries.title: Wi-Fi keeps dropping: keep taking payments
steps: Turn on the Offline Payments option so you can keep taking payments while not connected.
The payments are processed once the device is back online and logged in.
entries.quote: You can continue to take payments when you're not connected to the internet by turning on the Offline Payments option.

entries.title: Keep guests and other equipment off the Clover network
steps: Create two networks with different passwords: one for guests and one for the business.
Check your router manual if you are not sure how to create a guest network.
entries.quote: we recommend creating two networks, one for guests and one for business needs, with different passwords

entries.title: Avoid running Clover on a hotspot
steps: Avoid hotspots: they may be slower and cannot support many devices at once.
If you must use one, connect nothing to it except Clover devices.
entries.quote: If you absolutely must use a hotspot, don't connect anything to it besides Clover devices.

entries.title: Start a device replacement or return
steps: Replacements and returns both start by contacting support.
Have ready: Merchant ID (MID), device type and serial number, purchase date, and the reason for the return.
Support creates the shipping label for the device going back, and for a replacement also ships the new device.
entries.quote: For both replacements and returns, you need to initiate the process by contacting Clover support.
entries.note: Source says to contact Clover support.

entries.title: What to do on the device before returning or replacing it
steps: Sync all orders so no transactions are left pending.
Uninstall apps that have monthly fees so you are not charged again.
Deactivate the SIM card on a device that uses cellular data.
entries.quote: Sync all orders to ensure no transactions remain pending.

entries.title: Print the shipping label for a return or replacement
steps: After support has opened the return, log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Devices and printers.
Select the Devices tab and find the device you are returning.
In the manage column, select Print shipping label.
entries.quote: In the manage column, select Print shipping label.

entries.title: Pack a Clover device for return
steps: Put the device in a carton and pack it securely.
Include all cables, power supplies and accessories so you are not charged for missing parts.
Seal the carton and attach the printed shipping label.
Remove or cover any other label.
entries.quote: Make sure you include all cables, power supplies, and accessories to avoid being charged for missing parts.

entries.title: Ship a returned Clover device
steps: Write down the tracking number for each device you send back.
Schedule a UPS pickup or drop the package at a UPS location.
Track it at www.ups.com or by calling 1-800-PICK-UPS.
When it is received, the Devices and printers page on the dashboard updates.
entries.quote: Schedule a UPS pickup or drop off the package at a UPS location.

entries.title: Activate a replacement device
steps: Follow the steps on the new device to activate it.
If it asks for an activation code, find it on the Devices and printers page of your dashboard.
entries.quote: If you are prompted for an activation code, you can find the information on your dashboard, on the Devices and printers page.

entries.title: See all your Clover devices on the dashboard
steps: On the dashboard select Settings > View all settings.
In Business operations, select Devices and printers.
Select the Devices tab.
From there you can track a device order, replace a device, view device details, name a device, activate a device, or factory reset a device.
If your hardware is not listed, check you are logged in with the correct admin account or role.
entries.quote: The Devices tab displays a list of all Clover hardware and devices linked to your account
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Find the serial number, model and software version on the device
steps: Open the Device Settings app.
Scroll down and select About Device.
Read the serial number, model, software version and Reboot Time.
entries.quote: View details such as the serial number, model, and software version, and Reboot Time

entries.title: What the 8-digit activation code is
steps: A Clover device needs an 8-digit activation code before first use and after a factory reset.
It is unique to each device.
It is not the 4- or 6-digit passcode you log in with.
entries.quote: Clover devices require an 8-digit activation code before they can be used for the first time.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Find the device activation code
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard: the code is in a banner across the top of the home screen until the device is activated.
Check the business owner's email: the code is emailed when the device first connects to a network, and is also in the shipping notification email.
If the owner opted in, the code is also sent by text message; the partly masked phone number shows on the activation screen.
If you still cannot find it, contact support with your Merchant ID or Tax ID ready.
entries.quote: The activation code is displayed in a banner across the top of the dashboard home screen.

entries.title: Activation code after a factory reset
steps: After a factory reset the device needs a new activation code.
The new code is emailed to the business owner.
entries.quote: If an existing device requires a factory reset, a new activation code is sent to the owner via email.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Find your Merchant ID (MID) on the dashboard
steps: On the dashboard select Settings > View all settings.
Under About your business, select Business information.
The MID is at the top left of the page.
entries.quote: Under About your business, select Business information. Your MID is located at the top left of the page.

entries.title: Internet is down: will orders still reach the kitchen display?
steps: With Clover Local Connect, Clover devices on the same local network (Wi-Fi or wired) talk to each other directly.
An order taken at the register still shows on the KDS while the internet is down.
This is temporary: you still need the internet to process card payments and save sales data.
entries.quote: even if the internet is down, you can still take an order at the register on a Clover device, and it will show up on the Clover KDS

entries.title: Set up the network so the KDS keeps working offline
steps: Use a dedicated router for the Clover devices and connect it to the modem from your internet provider.
Use wired Ethernet to the router where possible; Wi-Fi, wired, or a mix all work.
If you mix Wi-Fi and wired, use only one router for the Clover network.
Need more wired ports: add Ethernet switches.
Need more Wi-Fi coverage: add an access point, not another router.
Connect nothing but Clover devices to that network and keep customers and guests off it.
entries.quote: If you are using Wi-Fi and need to cover a large area, add an additional Access Point, not another router.

entries.title: KDS on a mixed Wi-Fi and wired network: one router only
steps: When some Clover devices are on Wi-Fi and some are wired, there must be a single router for the Clover network.
entries.quote: When using a combination of Wi-Fi and wired networking, there must be only a single router for your Clover network.

entries.title: Read the Kitchen operations report
steps: On the dashboard select Reports > Kitchen operations.
Pick the date range: today, this week, or this month.
The report shows item volume per hour, average preparation and fulfillment times, items prepared per station, and the slowest items.
entries.quote: From the left, select Reports > Kitchen operations.

entries.title: Kitchen operations report is blank
steps: The report only has data for merchants using the Kitchen Display System.
If you only use a kitchen printer and have not set up a KDS, the report is blank.
entries.quote: Merchants who use only the Kitchen Printer and have not configured a KDS will see a blank report.

entries.title: Replace a lost or damaged power cord, cable or hub
steps: Work out which power cord, USB cable, Ethernet cable or hub is missing or damaged.
Contact support to buy the correct replacement part.
entries.quote: To order replacements for your device, card reader, or terminal, please contact customer support to purchase the correct part.
entries.note: Source says to contact customer support to buy the part.

entries.title: Look after cables and hubs
steps: Label each cable so it is easy to reconnect if unplugged.
Check cables and hubs for wear from time to time and replace them before they fail.
entries.quote: Periodically check cables and hubs for signs of wear and replace them before they fail.

entries.title: Bring a connected order (kitchen) printer online
steps: Make sure the Clover device is plugged in, on your network and activated, and that an accessory printer is plugged in and on the same network.
On the Clover device, open the Printers app.
Select Add in the lower right corner.
Tap Order printer; a list of printers on your Clover network appears.
Tap the printer to add. It then shows in the list of online printers.
Repeat for each further printer, one at a time.
entries.quote: Tap Order printer. A list of printers connected to your Clover network appears.

entries.title: Choose which items print on an order printer
steps: In the Printers app, find the printer under Order printer and tap it.
Under Labels to auto-print, tick the label, such as Kitchen or Bar.
Items with those labels print to this printer automatically.
entries.quote: Under Labels to auto-print, select the checkbox next to the label, such as Kitchen, Bar, or other custom label.

entries.title: Order does not print on the kitchen or order printer
steps: Confirm the labels are assigned correctly.
Check that the printer is online.
Make sure the Clover device and the printer are on the same network.
entries.quote: Make sure both the device and printer are on the same network.

entries.title: Test an order printer after setup
steps: Create a test order with items that carry the printer label (for example Kitchen or Bar).
Send the order. It should print on the chosen order printer.
entries.quote: Create a test order with items assigned to the appropriate printer label (for example, Kitchen, Bar, Station).

entries.title: Stop an order printer printing for a while
steps: Go to the printer itself.
Switch off its power.
entries.quote: On the printer, switch off the power.

entries.title: Remove a printer from your Clover device
steps: On the Clover device, open the Printers app.
Tap the printer name.
Tap Delete at the top right.
entries.quote: At the top right, tap Delete.

entries.title: Use the PIN Entry Aid for a customer with a visual disability (Flex Pocket)
steps: When the Enter PIN screen appears, place the PIN Entry Aid on top of the device and wrap its corners around the corners of the device.
If the customer would rather run the card as credit, press Skip and remove the aid.
Hand the device to the customer to enter the PIN.
A tone tells the customer the PIN was submitted and the card can be removed.
Remove the aid and finish the transaction.
Keep the aid stored close to the device.
entries.quote: The customer will hear a tone indicating their PIN was successfully submitted and they can remove their card.
entries.note: Source names the Flex 3 and Flex Pocket.

entries.title: Use the PIN Entry Aid on a Mini 3
steps: On the Enter PIN screen, press the Accessible PIN entry button.
Place the aid on the device with its top lined up with the top of the screen, so Cancel, Clear and Enter line up with the buttons.
Rotate the screen to the customer to enter the PIN.
A tone tells the customer the PIN was submitted and the card can be removed.
Rotate the Mini back, remove the aid and continue as the screen prompts.
To go on without the aid at any time, press Use screen and remove it.
entries.quote: Press the Accessible PIN entry button on your Mini 3 when you reach the Enter PIN screen during your transaction.

entries.title: Where to keep the Mini 3 PIN Entry Aid
steps: Keep it close to the Mini 3.
Clover suggests attaching it to the Mini's charging cable with the lanyard provided.
entries.quote: We encourage you to keep the PIN Entry Aid attached to your Mini’s charging cable for consistent storage and quick access.

entries.title: Start accessibility mode for a visually impaired cardholder (Flex 4, Flex Pocket)
steps: Set the volume to a comfortable level.
On the Present card screen, turn on the Accessibility mode option.
The device speaks the amount and tells the cardholder to tap or insert the card.
After the card is inserted, the device reads out the accessibility options.
The customer slides a finger down the screen to hear each option and double-taps anywhere to choose the last one announced.
entries.quote: On the Present card screen, activate the Accessibility mode option for the cardholder.

entries.title: Accessibility mode: where the sound comes from
steps: If wired headphones are connected, the audio plays through them.
Otherwise it plays through the device speakers.
entries.quote: If wired headphones have been connected then the audio will be through the headphones

entries.title: Accessibility mode: PIN entry with the tactile overlay
steps: If the customer asks, place the tactile overlay precisely over the screen.
The device speaks the amount and describes the PIN pad layout.
The customer enters the PIN using the overlay; each digit is confirmed by a sound.
The customer presses Enter and the payment goes through as normal.
entries.quote: Upon the customer's request, place the physical tactile overlay template precisely over the device screen.

entries.title: Accessibility mode: practice PIN entry
steps: Practice mode lets a customer learn the layout before paying.
The customer must never enter a real PIN in practice mode, because every digit is spoken aloud.
After the practice entry the customer returns to the accessibility options to make the real payment.
entries.quote: Customers must never use their real PIN during practice mode, as all digits entered in training mode are spoken aloud through the audio interface.

entries.title: Phone or tablet needed for the Clover Go app
steps: The Clover Go app needs iOS 11 or higher, or Android 6 or higher.
Download it from the App Store or Google Play.
entries.quote: To use the Clover Go app you need: iOS 11 or higher Android 6 or higher

entries.title: Turn on location sharing before taking payments in the Go app
steps: Turn on location sharing on the phone or tablet.
Clover uses the location of transactions to protect against fraud.
entries.quote: Turn on location sharing: Clover uses the location of transactions to protect against fraudulent activity.

entries.title: Clover Go card reader does not offer tips
steps: In the U.S., card readers are preset to either accept or reject tips.
If yours is not preset to accept tips and you want them, contact support.
entries.quote: If your card reader isn't preset to accept tips and you want to accept them, contact customer support.

entries.title: Log in to the Clover Go app for the first time
steps: Open the Go app and tap Get Started.
Enter your Clover account email and password and tap Log In.
If two-factor authentication is on, enter the code sent to you.
If you have more than one location, pick one and tap Continue.
Enter the passcode for your Clover account. The Home screen appears.
entries.quote: Open the Go app on your phone or tablet and tap Get Started.

entries.title: Forgot the Clover Go app password
steps: On the login screen tap Forgot Password.
A password reset is sent to your Clover account email.
entries.quote: If you don't have your password, tap Forgot Password, and we'll send a password reset to your Clover account email.

entries.title: Go app asks for email and password again
steps: After the first login you normally only need your passcode, fingerprint or face recognition.
If you log out, or do not use the app for seven days, you must log in again with email, password and passcode.
entries.quote: If you log out of the Go app or don't use it for seven (7) days, you'll need to log in again

entries.title: Find your passcode for the Go app
steps: On the dashboard select Employees > Employee List.
Select your name, then Edit Employee, to see your profile and passcode.
entries.quote: Select your name from the list and select Edit Employee to display your employee profile and your passcode.

entries.title: Reach Clover's live support from the device
steps: On a Clover device, tap Help on the home screen.
In the Clover Go app, open the menu and tap Help.
Your direct support phone number is printed on your statement.
entries.quote: On a Clover device, tap Help on the home screen.

entries.title: What a tamper alert means
steps: Clover devices have sensors that detect misuse or harm; if tampering is detected the device locks PIN-entry transactions.
In rare cases a drop or a shake can trigger it.
Clover emails you when a tamper is detected.
Contact support.
entries.quote: In rare cases, tampering may be detected if a device is dropped or shaken.

entries.title: Device tampered, return to manufacturer
steps: This can appear on the Get Help screen during setup.
The message cannot be cleared: the device has to be replaced.
Contact support for a replacement device.
entries.quote: you might be automatically directed to the Get Help screen with the error Device tampered, return to manufacturer.

entries.title: Tamper Detected
steps: This screen can appear in the Setup Wizard, or as an error in the Sale, Refund and other apps after activation.
The only way to remove it is to get a new device.
Contact support for a replacement.
entries.quote: The only way to remove the tampered message is to request a new device from Clover support.

entries.title: What still works on a tampered device
steps: PIN-entry payments are disabled.
You can still take transactions that do not need a PIN, and take orders, run reports and sync with other Clover devices.
Replace the device as soon as possible to get full payment function back.
entries.quote: However, PIN-entry payments are disabled.

entries.title: Request a replacement for a tampered Station, Mini or Flex from the device
steps: You must be an owner or admin.
Open the Setup app.
Tap Payments, then PIN Entry, then Prompt for PIN.
Tap Save.
Tap 'I need to accept PIN payments, please send me a replacement Clover device that accepts PIN payments'.
Tap OK.
You get an email with the activation code and tracking details when the replacement ships.
Activate the new device, then send the tampered one back in the same box using the return label inside.
entries.quote: Tap 'I need to accept PIN payments, please send me a replacement Clover device that accepts PIN payments'.

entries.title: Cost of replacing a tampered device
steps: If the device is still in warranty the replacement is free of charge.
Shipping and handling fees may apply.
entries.quote: If the device is still within the warranty period, the replacement device is provided free of charge.

entries.title: Clover Go reader: suspected tampering message in the Go app
steps: On a Go G3 reader a message in the Clover Go app says tampering is suspected, and an email is sent to the account address.
The reader can no longer take payments.
Contact support for a replacement reader.
Meanwhile you can still take payments in the Go app by scanning or keying the card, where available.
entries.quote: Clover Go G3. A message appears in the Clover Go app indicating suspected tampering

entries.title: Clover Go G2 reader lights flash in a random pattern
steps: Random flashing lights on a Go G2 reader mean a tamper was detected.
The reader can no longer take payments and must be replaced.
Contact support for a replacement.
entries.quote: Clover Go G2. Lights on the card reader flash in a random pattern.

entries.title: Inspect a device for signs of tampering
steps: Look for cutting, disassembly, broken seals or broken ports on the outside.
Look for unusual wires or overlays in the chip slot or near the PIN area.
Check for loose wires, broken connectors, a different number of connections, or cables of a different color.
Notice any change in resistance when inserting or removing a card.
Check whether the device has moved, has scratches around the display seams, or has missing or peeling Clover labels.
If you suspect tampering, contact support.
entries.quote: There are unusual wires or overlays connected inside the chip card slot, on or near the PIN-entry area.

entries.title: Should I factory reset my Clover device?
steps: Do not factory reset unless support tells you to, or you are cancelling the account or receiving a replacement.
A reset erases all data on the device, including transactions stored while offline.
The old activation code stops working; a new one is emailed and shown when you log in to your Clover account.
entries.quote: Do not factory reset Clover devices and equipment unless directed to by Clover customer support.

entries.title: Factory reset deletes offline transactions
steps: Transactions stored while offline are deleted by a factory reset.
Transactions that were accepted but not yet batched are saved before being removed from the device.
entries.quote: Any transactions stored while offline are also deleted, but transactions that were accepted but not batched are saved before being deleted from the device.

entries.title: Factory reset from the Setup app (only when support directs)
steps: Open the Setup app on the device to reset.
Tap Devices and select the device you are using.
Tap Factory Reset and tick the box confirming that all offline transactions on the device will be deleted.
Afterwards follow the on-screen steps to activate and connect the device.
entries.quote: Tap Factory Reset and then select the checkbox to confirm that you understand all offline transactions on the device will be deleted.

entries.title: Factory reset from the Settings app (only when support directs)
steps: Open the Settings app, or swipe down from the top right of the screen and select Settings.
Tap Reset, then Factory data reset.
Tap Reset Device to confirm.
entries.quote: Tap Reset; then tap Factory data reset.

entries.title: Factory reset a device from the dashboard (only when support directs)
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings, then Devices and printers, then the Devices tab.
Find the device and select device details.
Select Factory Reset and confirm that all data and unprocessed orders on the device will be lost.
entries.quote: A message appears requiring you to confirm the reset and acknowledge that all data and unprocessed orders on the device will be lost.

entries.title: Frozen Station Solo or Station Duo: hard reboot
steps: Unplug the display cord from the bottom of the Station.
Wait 10 seconds.
Plug the display cord back in.
Let the device reboot, then log in.
If it does not restart, contact support.
entries.quote: Unplug the display cord from the bottom of the Station.

entries.title: Frozen Mini: hard reboot
steps: Unplug the power cord from the Mini hub.
Open the paper door and take out the paper roll.
Hold the green reset button at the back of the paper roll cavity for a full 15 seconds.
Plug the power cord back into the hub. The Clover logo appears.
If it does not restart, contact support.
entries.quote: Remove the paper roll, then hold the green reset button located at the back of the printer roll cavity for 15 full seconds.

entries.title: Frozen Flex or Flex Pocket: hard reboot
steps: Take the device off its charging cradle or unplug the power cord.
Hold the power button down for 32 seconds, then release.
Press the power button again until the Clover image appears.
Put it back on the cradle or reconnect the power cord.
Enter your passcode when asked.
If it does not restart, contact support.
entries.quote: Hold the power button down for 32 seconds, then release.

entries.title: Frozen Compact: hard reboot
steps: Unplug the display cord from the bottom of the Compact.
Wait 10 seconds.
Plug the cord back in.
Let it reboot, then log in.
If it does not restart, contact support.
entries.quote: Unplug the display cord from the bottom of the Compact.

entries.title: Device does not restart after a hard reboot
steps: If the device does not restart after the hard reboot steps for its model, contact support.
entries.quote: If your device doesn't restart, contact Clover support.

entries.title: Why the device restarts by itself every day
steps: Clover devices reboot automatically every 24 hours for performance and security.
It takes about 1 to 2 minutes.
All settings and data, including offline payments, are kept.
By default it happens at a random time between 3 am and 5 am local time.
entries.quote: Clover devices automatically reboot every 24 hours.

entries.title: Clover Needs to Reboot
steps: This notice appears one minute before the daily reboot, with a 60-second countdown.
Do nothing and it reboots after the countdown.
Tap Cancel to put it off until the next day.
Tap Change Reboot Time to pick another time.
Tap Reboot Now to reboot at once.
entries.quote: One minute before rebooting, your device notifies you that Clover Needs to Reboot and starts a 60-second countdown:

entries.title: Change the daily automatic reboot time
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the home screen and tap the Settings icon.
Tap About device at the bottom of the list.
Tap Reboot time.
Set the time on the clock and tap Done.
entries.quote: Use the clock to change the time; then tap Done.

entries.title: Device did not do its daily reboot
steps: If the device was manually rebooted within 6 hours before the reboot time, it skips the automatic reboot that day.
It reboots the next day at the usual time.
entries.quote: If your device manually rebooted within 6 hours before the reboot time, the system will not reboot again on that day.

entries.title: Connect a Clover device to Wi-Fi from Settings
steps: Open the Settings app.
In Wireless & Networks, tap WiFi.
If WiFi is off, slide the switch to ON; a list of networks appears.
Select your network, or search for it by name.
Enter the network password.
When connected, the network name shows a status of Connected.
entries.quote: When a connection is established, the network name appears with a status of Connected.

entries.title: Wi-Fi signal is weak
steps: Check the network status icons at the top of the screen for connection and signal strength.
If the Wi-Fi signal is low, move the device to a different spot and see whether it improves.
entries.quote: If the WiFi signal strength is low, try moving to a different location to see if the signal strength improves.

entries.title: Older device on the AT&T 3G network cannot take payments
steps: AT&T shut down its 3G network on February 28, 2022.
A device that only used AT&T 3G must be connected to Wi-Fi (or Ethernet for a 3G Mini), or be replaced with a 4G device.
For a 3G Mini: connect an Ethernet cable to the hub, open Settings and check the network is connected.
entries.quote: AT&T is shutting down its 3G network on February 28, 2022.
entries.note: Applies to older 3G units, not current models.

entries.title: When a simple restart (soft reboot) helps
steps: Restart the device to fix random network dropouts.
Restart it to improve slow performance.
Restart it so settings you just changed take effect.
entries.quote: Correcting random network dropouts

entries.title: Restart (soft reboot) a Station
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen.
Tap Reboot, then tap Reboot again when asked.
The Station powers off for a moment and turns back on by itself.
entries.quote: The Station Duo powers off momentarily and then turns on again on its own.

entries.title: Restart (soft reboot) a Mini or Flex
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen.
Tap Reboot, then tap Reboot again when asked.
The device powers off for a moment and turns back on by itself.
entries.quote: The Mini and Flex power off momentarily and then turns on again on its own.

entries.title: Restart (soft reboot) a Compact
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen.
Tap Reboot, then tap Reboot again when asked.
The Compact powers off for a moment and turns back on by itself.
entries.quote: The Compact powers off momentarily and then turns on again on its own.

entries.title: Restart a Kiosk running in Kiosk mode
steps: Press and hold the Clover logo in the lower-left corner of the screen.
Enter the admin passcode.
Select Exit Kiosk Mode.
Press and hold the device power button until the power menu appears.
Tap Reboot, then Reboot again when asked.
If Restart is not offered, select Power off, wait about 10 seconds, then press the power button to turn the Kiosk back on.
entries.quote: If Restart is not available, select Power off, wait about 10 seconds, then press the power button again to turn the Kiosk back on.

entries.title: Restart a customer-facing Kiosk device in a tethered setup
steps: Tap the four corners of the screen to leave customer-facing mode.
Enter the admin passcode on the lock screen.
Tap Reboot, then Reboot again when asked.
entries.quote: Tap the four corners of the screen to exit customer-facing mode.

entries.title: Cannot get to device settings on a customer-facing Kiosk
steps: In a tethered setup the customer-facing device runs a full-screen app that blocks device settings.
Tap the four corners of the screen and enter the admin passcode to leave customer-facing mode first.
entries.quote: the customer-facing device runs a full-screen application that prevents access to device settings until you exit customer-facing mode using the four-corner tap gesture and enter the admin passcode

entries.title: Do not pull cables from a Station while it is on
steps: Do not remove cables while the Station is powered on.
Removing the display cable (green sticker) while on can permanently damage the device.
USB devices plugged into the bottom of the printer can be added and removed while it is on.
entries.quote: Removing the display cable (marked with a green sticker and indicator) can permanently damage the device.
entries.note: Written about the original Clover Station; the hard-reboot article for Station Solo/Duo does tell you to unplug the display cord. The two Clover articles differ.

entries.title: Station does not recognize a newly plugged-in USB device
steps: USB devices can be plugged into the bottom of the printer while the Station is on.
Reboot the Station so it recognizes the new USB device.
entries.quote: You may need to reboot the Clover Station for it to recognize new USB devices.

entries.title: Screen is dark: the device may be asleep
steps: Clover devices are meant to stay powered on.
When idle the device goes to sleep; tap the touchscreen to wake it.
It also restarts by itself every 24 hours and may restart after a software update.
entries.quote: When not in use, your device enters sleep mode and wakes when you tap the touchscreen.

entries.title: Turn a Clover device off (general rule)
steps: On most devices, hold the power button for more than 10 seconds until a menu with a shut down option appears.
A device with no power button is powered down by unplugging it for 10 seconds.
entries.quote: Devices without a power button can be powered down by unplugging for 10 seconds.

entries.title: Turn off a Flex or Flex Pocket
steps: From the home screen, swipe down from the top right. A power button appears.
Press the power button until the screen asks to Shut Down.
Confirm Shut Down.
entries.quote: Press the power button until the screen displays a prompt to Shut Down.

entries.title: Turn off a Kitchen Display
steps: Find the power button on the bottom of the device.
Press and hold it for a few seconds until the device begins to shut down.
entries.quote: Locate the power button on the bottom of the device.

entries.title: Turn off a Kiosk
steps: Find the power button on the back of the Kiosk.
Press and hold it for a few seconds until the device begins to shut down.
entries.quote: Locate the power button which is located on the back of the Kiosk.

entries.title: Turn off a Mini
steps: From the home screen, swipe down from the top right. A green power button appears.
Press the power button until the screen asks to Shut Down.
Confirm Shut down.
entries.quote: From the home screen, swipe down from the top-right. A green power button appears.

entries.title: Turn off a Station Solo
steps: Find the power button on the right side at the back of the main display.
Press and hold it for a few seconds until a menu appears.
Select Shut Down and confirm if asked.
Wait a few moments for it to power down.
entries.quote: Locate the power button which is on the right side at the back of the main display.

entries.title: Turn off a Station Duo (both screens)
steps: Find the power button on the right side at the back of both the main display and the customer-facing display.
Press and hold both power buttons at the same time until menus appear on both screens.
Select Shut Down on both displays and confirm if asked.
Allow a few minutes for both displays to power down.
entries.quote: Press and Hold simultaneously the power button on both the main display and the customer-facing display until menus appear on both screens.

entries.title: Turn off a Compact
steps: From the home screen, swipe down from the top right (near the clock). A power button appears on the screen.
Press the power button until the screen asks to Shut Down.
Confirm Shut Down.
entries.quote: From the home screen, swipe down from the top-right of the device (near the clock), a power button will appear on the screen.

entries.title: Turn off a Clover Go reader
steps: Find the power button on the right side of the reader.
Press it.
When the reader is off, the blue status light goes out.
entries.quote: When the device is off, the blue status light turns off.

entries.title: Check for and install a software update on the device
steps: Make sure the device is on a stable Wi-Fi network.
Swipe down from the top right and tap Settings > System > Check for system updates.
In System Updates, tap Update Now. The download starts.
Follow the on-screen prompts. The device may restart several times.
After it reboots, go to Settings > Device Settings > System Updates to confirm the update installed.
entries.quote: From the top right, swipe down, tap Settings > System > Check for system updates.

entries.title: Device keeps restarting during an update
steps: It is normal for the device to restart several times while an update installs.
Follow the on-screen prompts until it finishes.
entries.quote: Your device may restart several times during this process.

entries.title: What to do with an old Flex or Flex Pocket battery
steps: The battery is a rechargeable lithium-ion battery.
Recycle the old battery properly; do not put it in the trash.
Clover points to the EPA guidelines on used batteries.
entries.quote: Once the new battery is installed in your Flex device, the old battery should be recycled properly.

entries.title: Clean a Clover device safely
steps: Turn the device off and unplug it.
Use only a soft, lint-free cloth such as microfiber.
Dampen the cloth with water to wipe off dirt and smudges.
Dampen the cloth with 70% to 90% isopropyl alcohol to disinfect the unit and touchscreen.
Never spray anything directly on the device; spray the cloth.
Keep liquid away from openings, buttons, seams and the card slots; use a dry cloth there.
Do not use abrasive cleaners or solvents.
Let the unit dry before switching it back on.
entries.quote: Do not spray anything directly on the device; spray on the cloth.

entries.title: Cleaning around the card readers
steps: Avoid getting alcohol or water into or around the places where cards are inserted, tapped or swiped.
If those areas need cleaning, use a dry cloth.
entries.quote: If you need to clean those areas, make sure the cloth you use is dry.

entries.title: Clean a greasy Kitchen Display
steps: Turn the KDS off and unplug it from the outlet.
Wipe the screen and power cable gently with a soft, dry cloth. Do not use paper towels or abrasive materials.
For remaining grease, use a microfiber cloth slightly dampened with water or isopropyl alcohol (disinfecting wipes without bleach are fine).
Keep water and cleaner out of openings and ports; use very little liquid and dry the screen straight away.
Brush debris gently from the screen edges and the cable plugs with a soft-bristled brush, then wipe.
Dry the cable with a dry cloth; never with heat or a hair dryer.
entries.quote: Avoid using paper towels or abrasive materials that can scratch the screen.

entries.title: Kitchen Display cable is frayed or damaged
steps: After cleaning, check the cable for frayed or exposed wires.
If the cable is damaged, replace it immediately to avoid electric shock or fire.
entries.quote: If the cable is damaged, replace it immediately to prevent the risk of electric shock or fire.

entries.title: Dirt and grease can stop a Kitchen Display working properly
steps: In a kitchen, touchscreens and cables get dirty and greasy, which can affect how they work.
Clean the touchscreen regularly to stop build-up.
entries.quote: In a kitchen environment, electronic devices, especially touchscreens and cables, can become dirty and greasy, which can affect their functionality.

entries.title: Change the language on a Clover device
steps: Open the Settings app.
Select System and tap Languages & input.
Select Languages, then Add a language, and choose the language.
Move that language to position 1 in the list.
Return to the home screen to see the new language.
entries.quote: To activate your preferred language, move the language to the 1 position in Languages.

entries.title: Remove a language from a Clover device
steps: Open the Settings app.
Select System, tap Languages & input, then Languages.
Tap the three dots at the top right.
Select Remove, choose the language, and tap the trash icon.
Select OK.
entries.quote: Select Remove and choose the language you wish to remove, and tap the trash icon in the top right corner.

entries.title: Using the SIM card (cellular data) on a Clover device
steps: Some Clover devices have a SIM card you can activate to use cellular data instead of Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
You must enable data service and are billed monthly for it.
SIM cards are now managed in the device and account settings, not the Wireless Manager app.
entries.quote: To use a SIM card, you'll need to enable data service and will be billed monthly for access to the service.

entries.title: Activate or deactivate the SIM card on the device
steps: You need permission to open the Setup app.
Connect the device to the internet by Wi-Fi or Ethernet first.
Open the Setup app.
Select Cellular data or Mobile data, whichever you see.
Find the SIM card and select Activate or Deactivate.
If data service is not yet enabled, accept the service terms when asked.
After activating, turn off Wi-Fi and Ethernet to check the device connects over cellular.
entries.quote: Find the SIM card you want to manage and select Activate or Deactivate.

entries.title: Activate or deactivate a SIM card from the dashboard
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Cellular data or Mobile data.
Find the SIM card and select Activate or Deactivate.
entries.quote: Under Business operations, select Cellular data or Mobile data, depending on what you see.

entries.title: Check how the device is connected to the internet
steps: Open the Device settings.
Select Network & Internet.
entries.quote: To check how the device is connected to the internet, open the Device settings and select Network & Internet.

entries.title: Before deactivating a SIM that is in use
steps: Connect the device to the internet another way first, such as Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
entries.quote: Before deactivating a SIM card that is currently in use, connect the device to the internet using another connection method, such as Wi‑Fi or Ethernet.

entries.title: Manage the SIM card on a Kiosk
steps: Leave Kiosk mode first: press and hold the Clover logo in the lower-left corner, enter the admin passcode, and select Exit Kiosk mode.
On a tethered customer-facing device instead: tap the four corners of the screen and enter the admin passcode.
Open the Setup app and select Cellular data or Mobile data.
Select the SIM card and tap Activate or Deactivate.
Return to the Home screen and open the Clover Kiosk app to go back into Kiosk mode.
entries.quote: If the device was previously running in Kiosk mode, open the Clover Kiosk app to resume Kiosk mode.

entries.title: What's in the Flex Pocket box
steps: The box holds the Flex Pocket and a power adaptor.
A free PIN entry aid can be requested from Clover support.
entries.quote: To request a free PIN entry aid, contact Clover support.

entries.title: Network needed before activating a Flex Pocket
steps: Have your Wi-Fi router set up and connected to the internet before you start.
The network must use WPA or WPA2 security and be a closed, protected network.
entries.quote: Before activating, make sure your WiFi router is set up, connected to the internet, and has a security level of WPA or WPA2.

entries.title: Activate a new Flex Pocket
steps: Peel the protective plastic film off the screen.
Press the power button on the right side until the Clover logo appears.
Choose your language.
Enter your Wi-Fi network details to get online.
If Wi-Fi is not available and the device has a SIM card, choose the cellular option offered.
When asked for an activation code, follow the on-screen instructions to get it and enter it. Clover then installs the latest apps.
Continue through the remaining screens.
entries.quote: Switch on the device by pressing the power button on the right side until the Clover logo appears.

entries.title: Flex Pocket: no Wi-Fi available during setup
steps: If Wi-Fi is not available and the device has a SIM card, the setup screen offers a cellular network option.
Choose it to connect over cellular.
entries.quote: If WiFi is unavailable and your device has a SIM card, you'll see an option for connecting to a cellular network.

entries.title: Flex Pocket setup did not ask me to set a passcode
steps: During activation you normally get the chance to set a passcode.
If you already have an admin account, activation skips this step.
Passcodes can be set on the dashboard or in the Employees app on the device.
entries.quote: If you already have an admin account, the activation process will not include this step.

entries.title: Replace the Flex Pocket battery
steps: Turn the device off.
Use a 1.5mm hex key or hex screwdriver to remove the two screws on the back.
Lift the battery door off from the bottom first.
Pull the tab downward and then upward to release the battery.
Detach the battery cord from the device.
Attach the new battery's cord.
Slide the bottom of the battery into the device first.
Refit the battery door: slide the A side in first, then push down to snap the B side in.
Put the 2 screws back.
entries.quote: Pull the tab downward, and then upward, to release the battery.

entries.title: Change the SIM card in a Flex Pocket
steps: The Flex Pocket comes with a SIM card already installed; you can swap in your own.
Turn the device off.
Use a 1.5mm hex key or hex screwdriver to remove the two screws on the back.
Lift the battery door off from the bottom.
Pull the tab downward and then upward to release the battery, and detach the battery cord.
Remove and replace the SIM card.
Reattach the battery cord and slide the bottom of the battery in first.
Refit the battery door (A side first, then snap down the B side) and the 2 screws.
entries.quote: To access the SIM card, you'll need to remove the battery from the device first.

entries.title: Flex or Flex Pocket not charging: first checks
steps: Use the original Clover charging cable and adapter.
Make sure the charging port and cradle are clean and free of debris.
Check there is no physical damage to the device, cradle or cable.
Make sure the cable is plugged in correctly.
entries.quote: Make sure you are using the original Clover charging cable and adapter.

entries.title: Flex battery very low or completely drained
steps: Charge the device for at least 30 minutes before turning it on.
Charge until the battery is at least 20% before using it.
entries.quote: If the battery is very low or fully drained, charge the device for at least 30 minutes before turning it on.

entries.title: Flex battery drains quickly
steps: Turn on Battery saver in Settings.
Do not keep the device connected to power all the time; let the battery charge and discharge.
Do not leave it on the cradle for long periods when not in use.
entries.quote: If the battery drains quickly, enable Battery saver in Settings on your device.

entries.title: Protect a Flex from power fluctuations
steps: Plug the charger into a surge protector.
entries.quote: Use a surge protector to protect your device from power fluctuations.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Flashing red
steps: The device is not seated properly or is disconnected from the cradle.
Reposition the device on the cradle.
entries.quote: Flashing red The device is not properly seated or is disconnected from the cradle. Reposition the device on the cradle.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Solid red
steps: There is a charging error or something is obstructing the cradle.
Remove the device and check for debris.
entries.quote: Solid red Charging error or obstruction in the cradle. Remove the device and check for debris.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Blinking yellow
steps: A foreign object was detected on the cradle.
Remove any object from the cradle.
entries.quote: Blinking yellow Foreign object detected on the cradle. Remove any object from the cradle.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: No change in LEDs
steps: The device may not be getting power.
Restart the device while it is in the cradle.
entries.quote: No change in LEDs The device may not be receiving power. Restart the device while it is in the cradle.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Flashing green
steps: The device is charging.
Nothing to do.
entries.quote: Flashing green The device is charging. No action needed.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Solid green
steps: The device is fully charged.
Nothing to do.
entries.quote: Solid green The device is fully charged. No action needed.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Single blink red at power-on
steps: The cradle is finishing its startup calibration.
This may show briefly when the cradle powers on.
entries.quote: Single blink red The cradle is completing startup calibration.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Single blink yellow at power-on
steps: The cradle is finishing an internal reset.
This may show briefly when the cradle powers on.
entries.quote: Single blink yellow The cradle is completing an internal reset.

entries.title: Charging cradle LED: Solid yellow
steps: This is a rare internal error in the cradle.
Disconnect and reconnect the cradle.
If it continues, contact support.
entries.quote: If a startup error persists, disconnect and reconnect the cradle. If the issue continues, contact Clover support.
entries.note: The merchant can try reconnecting the cradle first; escalate if the light stays.

entries.title: Check whether a Flex is actually charging
steps: Plug the power adapter into an outlet you know works.
Connect the device to the charging adapter or cradle.
Flex 3 and Flex 4: the LED lights on the cradle show charging status.
Flex Pocket: plug a USB-C charger into the port on the top; a battery icon appears briefly.
Make sure the cable is firmly connected and the adapter gives enough power.
entries.quote: Flex 3 and Flex 4: LED lights on the cradle indicate charging status.

entries.title: Charge a Flex Pocket and confirm it is charging
steps: Connect a USB-C charger directly to the port on the top of the device.
A battery icon appears briefly to show it is charging.
The Flex Pocket has no charging cradle; the USB-C port is its only way to charge.
entries.quote: Flex Pocket: Connect a USB‑C charger directly to the port on the top of the device. A battery icon appears briefly to indicate it is charging.

entries.title: Flex on battery looks dead or unresponsive
steps: On battery power the device may be in power-saving mode and only look unresponsive.
Press and hold the Power button on the right side for about 30 seconds.
If nothing shows, press and hold the Power button for at least 1 minute but no more than 2 minutes to force it off and restart.
entries.quote: If nothing appears on the screen, press and hold the Power button for at least 1 minute (no more than 2 minutes) to force the device to power off and restart.
entries.note: Clover's hard-reboot article gives a different hold time (32 seconds).

entries.title: Flex not charging after sitting on the cradle a long time: reset the cradle
steps: Take the Flex off the cradle.
Unplug the power cable from the cradle.
Wait 30 to 60 seconds.
Plug the power cable back into the cradle.
Put the Flex back on the cradle.
entries.quote: This clears excess charge buildup and restores proper power flow.

entries.title: Flex charging cradle not working: charge directly
steps: Connect a USB-C fast charging cable straight to the device.
On Flex 3 and Flex 4 the charging port is on the top of the device.
entries.quote: If the cradle is not working, connect a USB-C fast charging cable directly to the device.

entries.title: Flex Pocket will not charge
steps: Try a different USB-C cable or power adapter.
Make sure the adapter gives adequate power.
The USB-C port on the top is the only way to charge; skip any cradle steps.
entries.quote: Try a different USB‑C cable or power adapter if the device does not charge.

entries.title: Flex charging: when to call support
steps: The device shows no charging indicator.
The device does not turn on after charging and restarting.
The battery does not hold a charge.
The cradle still shows an error after troubleshooting.
In these cases the device may need service or replacement; contact support.
entries.quote: The device does not turn on after charging and restarting.

entries.title: Why a Flex stops charging
steps: Usual causes: a loose connection, a faulty cable or adapter, debris on the cradle, or leaving the device on power all the time without letting the battery cycle.
entries.quote: Charging issues are typically caused by a loose connection, a faulty cable or adapter, debris on the cradle

entries.title: Keep a Flex battery healthy
steps: Charge and discharge the device regularly.
Keeping it connected to power continuously can stop normal battery cycling and cause charging problems.
entries.quote: Keeping the Flex continuously connected to power can prevent normal battery cycling and may cause charging issues.

entries.title: Store a Flex or Flex Pocket you will not use for a while
steps: Fully charge the device.
Power it off: press and hold the power button for 3 seconds and select Power Off on the screen.
Keep it out of direct sunlight and away from high humidity.
Keep it between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
It can be stored for up to 12 months; recharge it before storing longer.
entries.quote: You can store all Flex devices for 12 months before they need recharging.

entries.title: A fully flat Flex battery can lead to tamper mode
steps: The Flex has 2 batteries that together keep tamper detection powered.
A charged main battery keeps the device from going into tampered mode.
If the main battery fully discharges, the backup battery keeps tamper detection going for a further period.
If the backup battery also discharges, the device's ability to process transactions may be affected.
If that has happened, contact support.
entries.quote: When the backup battery discharges, the device's ability to process transactions may be affected.

entries.title: Replace the battery in a Flex with a replaceable battery
steps: Turn the Flex off.
Use a 1.5mm hex key or hex screwdriver to remove the two screws at the bottom of the device.
Lift the battery door off from the bottom.
Remove the two screws near the top of the battery and pull the battery gently down from the top.
Insert the new battery and refit the screws and cover.
Dispose of the old battery according to local regulations.
entries.quote: Remove the two screws near the top of the battery, then remove the battery by gently pulling down from the top of the battery.

entries.title: Change the SIM card in a Flex
steps: Turn the Flex off.
Use a 1.5mm hex key or hex screwdriver to remove the two screws at the bottom of the device.
Lift the battery door off from the bottom.
Remove the two screws near the top of the battery and pull the battery gently down from the top.
Slide the SIM card door to the left and lift it open.
Swap the SIM, with the notched corner of the card at the top right.
Put the battery back and refit all screws.
entries.quote: Remove the current SIM and replace it with your own, making sure the notched corner of the card is at the top right.

entries.title: Find the serial number on a Flex
steps: Open the receipt paper door.
Take out the paper.
Read the serial number (S/N) in the compartment; it starts with the letter C.
Have it ready if you call support.
entries.quote: Find the serial number (S/N) in the compartment.

entries.title: Tell which Flex generation you have
steps: Open the receipt paper door and remove any paper.
Read the model number: Flex 2 is C403, Flex 3 is C405, Flex 4 is C406.
entries.quote: The Flex 2 is C403, Flex 3 is C405, and Flex 4 is C406.

entries.title: What's in the Flex 4 box
steps: Flex with silicone sleeve, charging cradle, a receipt paper roll, power adaptor, and plugs for select regions.
A free PIN entry aid can be requested from Clover support.
entries.quote: Flex with silicone sleeve

entries.title: Where the card readers and scanner are on a Flex
steps: Insert chip cards into the chip card reader.
Slide cards through the magnetic stripe reader.
Customers tap cards, phones or watches on the contactless reader on the display screen.
To scan a barcode or QR code, hold the trigger down while pointing the Flex at it, and release when the screen shows it was processed.
entries.quote: Customers can tap chip cards, NFC-enabled phones, or watches on the contactless payment reader on the display screen.

entries.title: Charging a Flex without the cradle
steps: The USB-C charging port works with Clover's travel kit charger (sold separately) or any USB-C charging cable.
entries.quote: The USB-C charging port can be used with Clover’s travel kit power charger (available separately) or any USB-C charging cable.

entries.title: Activate a new Flex
steps: Make sure your Wi-Fi router is set up, online, and uses WPA or WPA2 security.
Peel the protective film off the screen.
Press the power button on the right side until the Clover logo appears.
Choose your language.
Enter your Wi-Fi details; if Wi-Fi is unavailable and the Flex has a SIM card, choose the cellular option.
Enter the activation code when asked, following the on-screen instructions to retrieve it. Clover installs the latest apps.
Continue through the remaining screens.
entries.quote: Connect the Flex to the internet by entering your WiFi network information.

entries.title: Load receipt paper in a Flex
steps: Hold the Flex with its back facing you.
Open the paper compartment by pulling the top of the door toward you.
Insert the roll so the end comes straight out of the slot at the top of the door.
Close the door until it clicks.
Tap on the screen to print a test receipt.
entries.quote: Insert the roll of paper so that the end extends straight out of the slot in the top of the compartment door.

entries.title: Set up the Flex charging cradle
steps: The Flex arrives with enough charge to set up and activate.
Hold the cradle upside down, push the cord from the power brick firmly into the charging port, and thread it across and out the back.
Plug the power cord into an outlet.
Set the Flex on top of the cradle.
Charge until the cradle lights turn solid green.
entries.quote: Allow the device to charge until the indicator lights on the cradle turn solid green.

entries.title: Flex not printing: check the paper roll
steps: Check the roll is installed correctly and has not run out.
Use thermal paper 2 1/4 inches wide by 85 feet long (5.7 cm by 25.9 m).
Make sure the paper is not jammed and is feeding.
entries.quote: Use thermal paper rolls measuring 2 1/4 inches wide by 85 feet long (5.7 cm by 25.9 m).

entries.title: Flex receipts faint or patchy: clean the print head
steps: Turn the device off and unplug it.
Gently clean the print head with a soft, lint-free cloth to remove dust or debris.
entries.quote: Use a soft, lint-free cloth to gently clean the print head to ensure there is no dust or debris obstructing it.

entries.title: Flex not printing: check printer status in Diagnostics
steps: On the home screen tap Diagnostics.
View the printer status and queue there.
Also check the printer settings in the device menu are set for receipt printing.
entries.quote: From there, you can view the printer status and queue.

entries.title: Flex still not printing: update and restart
steps: Make sure the device has the latest update installed.
Power the device off, wait a few minutes, and power it back on.
Check the receipt paper itself is not damaged or poor quality.
entries.quote: Restart device: Power off the device, wait a few minutes, and power it back on.

entries.title: Print a test receipt on a Flex
steps: Tap the Printers app.
Select your printer.
Tap Print test receipt.
entries.quote: On your Clover device, tap the Printers app.

entries.title: Replace the paper roll in a Flex
steps: Use thermal paper 2 1/4 inches (5.7 cm) wide by 85 feet (25.9 m) long.
Find the receipt paper door on the back of the device.
Open it by pulling the top of the door toward you.
Remove the empty roll.
Insert the new roll so the end comes straight out of the slot at the top of the door.
Close the door until it clicks.
Tap Print a Test Receipt on the screen.
entries.quote: On the display screen, tap Print a Test Receipt.

entries.title: Fit and adjust the Flex Extender
steps: A silicone sleeve must be on the Flex.
Snap the Flex into the cradle so customers can read the display; you feel a click.
Twist the extender to the left to unlock it.
Pull to lengthen it.
Twist to the right to lock it.
Take the Flex off the extender to charge it.
entries.quote: Charging port (disconnect the device from the extender to charge)

entries.title: Check whether a Mini can use cellular
steps: Open the printer lid on the back of the device.
If the tag says Clover Mini 3G, it is cellular-enabled.
If it says Clover Mini Wi-Fi, it is not; use Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
entries.quote: If you see the text Clover Mini Wi-Fi, your Clover Mini is not mobile-enabled.

entries.title: Flex is cellular-enabled out of the box
steps: The Flex comes with a SIM card installed, so it is enabled for cellular.
entries.quote: Clover Flex: Your device comes with an installed SIM card. This means it is enabled.

entries.title: Cellular not working: check the SIM card status
steps: Swipe down from the top right of the screen and tap Settings.
In Wireless & networks, tap More.
Tap Cellular networks, then Access Point Names.
SIM information for the active SIM is shown.
If you bought your own data plan, ask your carrier to confirm the SIM is GSM, active, and has data enabled.
entries.quote: Under Cellular network settings, tap Access Point Names.

entries.title: Own SIM card does not work in the Clover device
steps: Only GSM SIM cards work with Clover Mini and Flex.
A SIM labelled CDMA will not work.
entries.quote: If the SIM card is labelled CDMA, it will not work with the Clover device.

entries.title: New SIM not detected straight away
steps: A SIM enabled for the first time can take a minute or more to be detected.
In an area with spotty coverage it may never be detected.
entries.quote: it might take a minute or more for the SIM card to be detected

entries.title: Cellular icon greyed out or says no service
steps: Swipe down from the top right of the screen.
If Airplane mode is ON, tap it to switch it OFF.
If Wi-Fi is active and shows a network name, tap it OFF: Wi-Fi can interfere with cellular when both are on.
entries.quote: If the icon is grayed-out or says no service, check the airplane mode and Wi-Fi settings:

entries.title: Cellular stopped: data limit exceeded
steps: Swipe down from the top right and tap Settings.
Tap the cellular network and view data usage.
If the data limit has been exceeded, the cellular network is disabled; call your provider to raise the limit.
entries.quote: If your data usage limit has been exceeded, the 3G network will be disabled.

entries.title: No Wi-Fi: check Wi-Fi is switched on
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen and tap Settings.
Under Wireless & Networks, make sure Wi-Fi is ON; switch it on if not.
The device then searches for networks in range.
entries.quote: Under Wireless & Networks, check to make sure that Wi-Fi is switched ON.

entries.title: Device shows no Wi-Fi networks
steps: Check that the router from your internet provider is working.
Steady or blinking green router light: the router is working; move the Clover device and router closer together.
Router light blinking yellow or red: contact your internet provider.
entries.quote: If the router light blinks yellow or red, contact your ISP for help.

entries.title: Device warns about an unsecured Wi-Fi network
steps: Clover devices require a WPA2-secured Wi-Fi network.
If the device detects an unsecured network it may ask you to change to a secure one.
entries.quote: The Clover device may detect an unsecured network and prompt you to change your settings to a secure one.

entries.title: Wi-Fi network does not show Connected
steps: Find your network in the list and check it says Connected.
If not, tap it and enter the network password.
If you do not know the password, ask your internet provider or whoever set up the network.
entries.quote: Find the network you want to use and check to make sure it lists a Connected status.

entries.title: Check Wi-Fi signal strength on the device
steps: Tap the network name and look for a status of good or excellent.
If it is fair, poor or none, the device is struggling to connect.
Choose another Wi-Fi network or use Ethernet.
Test by opening any app.
entries.quote: If the signal strength is fair, poor, or shown as none, your Clover device is having problems connecting to the internet.

entries.title: Work out whether the Wi-Fi or the Clover device is at fault
steps: Connect a phone or laptop to the same network with the same password.
If it connects and can open a website such as help.clover.com, the network is working.
If it cannot connect, the problem is likely the router or network; contact your internet provider or IT person.
entries.quote: If you cannot connect, then your network issues may lie with the router or network, and not with the Clover device.

entries.title: Wi-Fi connection is inconsistent: forget unused networks
steps: Open the Settings app.
If Bluetooth or Ethernet is enabled and not used, switch them off.
Tap Wi-Fi.
Tap each network that is not your Clover network and tap Forget.
Repeat for every other network so the device only tries your Clover network.
entries.quote: In the dialog box, tap Forget to ignore the network.

entries.title: Network dropouts: reboot the device
steps: Reboot the device if you changed network settings and it has not picked them up.
Reboot if the signal drops out at random.
Reboot if the network works with some devices and not others.
entries.quote: Reboot the device to properly reconnect to the internet and fix signal interruptions.

entries.title: Router firewall may block the Clover device
steps: Check that your router is not trying to connect through a firewall.
Clover does not recommend particular routers.
entries.quote: Check to make sure that your router is not trying to connect through a firewall.

entries.title: Ethernet not working: check the settings
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner and tap Settings.
Under Wireless & Networks, make sure Ethernet is selected; switch it ON if not.
Switch the Wi-Fi slider OFF so the device is forced to use the Ethernet cable.
Tap the Ethernet tab to see the connection status, MAC address and IP address.
A message confirms a successful Ethernet connection.
entries.quote: Turning off the Wi-Fi connection forces the Clover device to connect via your Ethernet cable.

entries.title: Ethernet: check DHCP or static IP
steps: If your network uses a dynamic IP, make sure DHCP is selected.
If it uses a static IP, select Static and fill in the fields (Gateway, Subnet Mask, DNS1, DNS2) correctly.
Your internet provider can tell you which you have.
entries.quote: If the network uses a dynamic IP to connect, make sure DHCP is selected.

entries.title: Ethernet: clear proxy settings
steps: Proxy server settings can interfere with the Ethernet connection.
Tap the Proxy Settings option.
Clear the Proxy Settings fields.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: Proxy server settings can interfere with the Ethernet connection. We recommend removing them to avoid problems:

entries.title: Test that the device is online
steps: Go to the Home screen.
Tap the Help app.
If Help loads and its links open, the device is connected to the internet.
entries.quote: If the Help app loads and you can tap links to access content on Clover Help, then the Clover device is connected to the Internet.

entries.title: Ethernet connection is inconsistent
steps: Open the Settings app.
Switch off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi if they are enabled, so the device uses only the Ethernet connection.
Reboot the device.
entries.quote: Disabling your Wi-Fi ensures that your Clover device connects through your primary and most stable connection.

entries.title: Payments time out or devices do not sync: improve the network
steps: Use your own internet service rather than a shared network.
Keep music and video streaming off the Clover network.
Reduce the number of other devices on the network.
Use a wired high-speed connection such as DSL or cable rather than a hotspot, especially with more than one Clover device or a kitchen printer.
If you use a hotspot, dedicate it to Clover.
entries.quote: Unstable networks can cause transactions to temporarily halt, causing the network connection to time out and disconnect because the network waited too long for a response.

entries.title: Authentication Failed (enterprise Wi-Fi)
steps: On a WPA2-Enterprise network this can mean the security certificate has expired.
A new certificate must be uploaded in the dashboard and the setup repeated on the device.
This needs your network administrator.
entries.quote: If a certificate expires, your device will be unable to connect and may display an Authentication Failed message.

entries.title: Connect a Clover device to enterprise (WPA2-Enterprise) Wi-Fi
steps: This is an advanced feature that needs certificates from your network administrator.
First connect the device to the internet another way (hotspot, LTE or Ethernet).
In the dashboard go to Settings > View all settings > Enterprise Wi-Fi certificates and upload the certificates.
On the device open the Setup app, tap the Menu icon, then the Refresh icon to download them.
Install them from Settings > Security > More security settings > Encryption and credentials > Install a certificate > Wi-Fi certificate.
Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Internet, pick the enterprise network, set the options your network needs, and tap Connect.
entries.quote: Under Business operations, select Enterprise Wi-Fi certificates.
entries.note: Needs the merchant's own network administrator.

entries.title: Incompatible (enterprise Wi-Fi device list)
steps: The dashboard marks devices that do not support enterprise Wi-Fi as Incompatible.
entries.quote: The dashboard displays devices that don’t support this feature as Incompatible.

entries.title: Forget a saved enterprise Wi-Fi network
steps: Open the Setup app.
Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Internet.
Tap the saved enterprise network.
Tap Forget on the Network details page.
entries.quote: On the Network details page that appears, tap Forget.

entries.title: Cable up the Clover local network (Local Connect)
steps: Use ready-made Cat-5 or better Ethernet cables with RJ45 connectors, as short as possible (100 meters / 328 feet at most).
Connect the router jack labelled WAN or Internet to the modem.
Connect the Clover devices to the router's LAN or Ethernet ports.
If you run out of ports, connect an unmanaged Ethernet switch to a LAN port and plug the remaining devices into the switch.
entries.quote: Connect the router jack labeled WAN or Internet to the modem.

entries.title: Router settings Clover Local Connect needs
steps: Give this list to whoever manages your router.
Subnet mask 255.255.255.0; larger masks such as 255.255.0.0 do not work.
LAN DHCP server on, with a lease time of 120 minutes or more.
Keep NAT on.
Turn off AP Isolation, Client Isolation and VLANs, plus port forwarding, DMZ, parental controls, guest networks, UPnP and QoS.
If Wi-Fi is used, turn on WPA2 with a password and turn off MAC filtering.
entries.quote: Clover Local Connect will not operate with larger subnet masks, such as 255.255.0.0.
entries.note: Needs the merchant's own network or IT support.

entries.title: Orders do not reach the KDS when the internet is down
steps: Clover devices must be able to talk to each other directly on the local network.
Have your router checked: all isolation features (AP Isolation, Client Isolation, VLANs) must be off.
Use a dedicated router for the point-of-sale network, wired where possible.
entries.quote: To make sure devices can communicate directly, turn off all isolation features, including AP Isolation, Client Isolation, and VLANs.

entries.title: What Clover Local Connect does and does not do
steps: It lets devices such as a Mini or Station Duo fire orders to the KDS immediately even when the internet is down.
An internet connection is still needed to process payments and sync orders to the cloud.
entries.quote: Requires an active internet connection to complete actions, such as processing payments and syncing orders to the cloud.

entries.title: What's in the Kitchen Display box
steps: The Kitchen Display, power cords and a power brick.
A stand is not included.
entries.quote: Power cords and power brick

entries.title: Power a Kitchen Display from a wall outlet
steps: Take the Kitchen Display out of the box.
Connect the power brick to the base of the KDS.
Connect the power brick to the power cord.
Plug the power cord into a wall outlet.
Press the power button on the device to turn it on.
entries.quote: Connect the power brick to the base of the KDS

entries.title: Where the Kitchen Display power button is (setup article)
steps: The setup article says to power on by pressing the power button on top of the device.
entries.quote: Power on your KDS by pressing the power button on top of the device
entries.note: Clover's own articles disagree: the power-down and storage articles say the button is on the bottom of the device.

entries.title: Mount a Kitchen Display on a stand or wall mount
steps: The KDS takes VESA 100mm mounts: countertop stands, wall mounts and other stands.
The stand is not included with the display.
Follow the mounting instructions that came with your stand.
entries.quote: Follow the mounting instructions that came with your stand to attach the KDS.

entries.title: Use the Kitchen Display in Kitchen mode
steps: Kitchen mode shows in-progress items and courses.
Tap the open circle next to an item to mark it complete.
When all items are prepared, tap Mark Ready.
entries.quote: Once all items are prepared, tap Mark Ready to show the order as ready.

entries.title: Use the Kitchen Display in Expo mode
steps: Expo mode shows in-progress and ready items and orders.
Orders update as the kitchen prepares them.
When an order is marked Ready, review it and tap Mark Complete to clear the ticket.
entries.quote: Once an order is marked as Ready, review the order and tap Mark Complete to clear the ticket.

entries.title: Long tickets: switch the KDS between finger scrolling and buttons
steps: Tap the Settings icon in the top left corner of the KDS.
Scroll to Ticket interaction.
Choose Scrolling (the default, scroll with a finger) or Buttons (up and down buttons).
The choice saves automatically.
entries.quote: Buttons: Lets you navigate through a ticket using up / down buttons.

entries.title: Change how tickets are laid out on the KDS
steps: Tap the Settings icon in the top left corner of the KDS.
Scroll to Ticket layout.
Choose Full columns (best for large orders), Grid (best for multiple orders) or Dynamic layout (best for showing the whole ticket).
The choice saves automatically.
entries.quote: Scroll to Ticket layout and select your preferred ticket layout view:

entries.title: Why KDS tickets turn yellow or red
steps: Delay statuses are on by default.
A ticket turns yellow after 7 minutes and red after 10 minutes.
You can change these thresholds under Ticket timing in the KDS Settings.
entries.quote: Tickets approaching delay display as yellow after 7 minutes and in red after 10 minutes.

entries.title: Show a live timer or a timestamp on KDS tickets
steps: Tap the Settings icon in the top left corner of the KDS.
Scroll to Time settings.
Choose a timestamp of when the ticket was fired (the default) or a live timer that counts up from 0.
entries.quote: Display a live timer on the ticket. The timer will start at 0 and count up in seconds.

entries.title: Change when KDS tickets are flagged as late
steps: Tap the Settings icon in the top left corner of the KDS.
Scroll to Ticket timing and set the delay thresholds you want.
The choice saves automatically.
entries.quote: Scroll to Ticket timing and set your preferred delay thresholds.

entries.title: Show only certain order types (dine-in, take-out, delivery) on a KDS
steps: Filtering by order type is off by default.
Tap the Settings icon in the top left corner of the KDS.
Scroll to Filter tickets by order type and choose.
The choice saves automatically.
entries.quote: Scroll to Filter tickets by order type and select your preferred option.

entries.title: Some order types never show on the KDS
steps: Check the order-type filter: tap the Settings icon in the top left of the KDS and scroll to Filter tickets by order type.
Filtering is off by default, so someone may have limited the types shown.
entries.quote: Filtering by order type is turned off by default.

entries.title: Items jump to the bottom of a KDS ticket when tapped
steps: By default an item marked Ready slides to the bottom of the ticket.
To change it, tap the Settings icon, scroll to Other settings, and clear the checkbox.
This does not apply to coursed orders.
