entries.quote: it slides down to the bottom. Active items are available front and center. This is not applicable for coursed orders.

entries.title: Group identical items on KDS tickets
steps: Tap the Settings icon in the top left corner of the KDS and scroll to Other settings.
Tick 'Group identical items together'.
Five burgers then show as 'Burger × 5'.
entries.quote: Select the 'Group identical items together' checkbox to save screen space

entries.title: Special instructions do not show on KDS tickets
steps: Tap the Settings icon in the top left corner of the KDS and scroll to Other settings.
Tick 'Show custom items in tickets' so instructions such as 'No onions' appear.
entries.quote: Select the 'Show custom items in tickets' checkbox to display special instructions such as 'No onions' or 'Extra cheese'.

entries.title: Show guest numbers on the KDS (Expo mode)
steps: Tap the Settings icon and scroll to Other settings.
Tick 'Show guest number (Expo mode only)'.
Each dish then shows the guest number next to it.
entries.quote: Select the 'Show guest number (Expo mode only)' checkbox to match dishes with the correct guest

entries.title: Item names look shortened or different on the KDS
steps: By default the KDS shows the alternate name as a short name.
To hide alternate names, clear 'Use alternate inventory names' under Other settings.
To keep them, choose Show full names (multiple lines) or Show compact names (up to 2 lines).
entries.quote: To hide the alternate name, clear the 'Use alternate inventory names' checkbox.

entries.title: Close the Kitchen Display app (before a restart or power down)
steps: Tap the gear icon in the top left corner of the KDS.
In the top right corner of the Settings menu, tap Quit KDS app.
You return to the home screen.
entries.quote: In the top right corner of the Settings menu, tap Quit KDS app and you will be returned to the home screen.

entries.title: Bump bar with the Kitchen Display
steps: Both Clover KDS models support a bump bar.
It is useful to keep fingerprints off the screen or when the KDS is wall-mounted.
Setup steps are in Clover's KDS Bump Bar Guide.
entries.quote: Both Clover kitchen display system models support a bump bar.

entries.title: Power a Kitchen Display over the Ethernet cable (PoE)
steps: Check your network switch or router supports PoE (the KDS needs IEEE 802.3at PoE+) and that PoE is enabled on it.
Connect the Ethernet cable to the PoE switch or router and to the Ethernet port on the KDS, firmly at both ends.
The LCD lights up briefly when the KDS is getting power.
Hold the power button for 2 to 3 seconds to turn it on.
entries.quote: To turn the device on, hold the power button for 2 to 3 seconds.

entries.title: Kitchen Display gets no power over Ethernet
steps: Make sure the network switch or router supports PoE and that the PoE switch is enabled.
The KDS supports IEEE 802.3at PoE+.
Check the Ethernet cable is firmly connected at both ends.
Otherwise use the supplied Clover power adapter.
If it still fails, contact support.
entries.quote: Make sure that your network switch or router supports PoE and that the PoE switch is enabled.

entries.title: Choose which orders show on each Kitchen Display
steps: Make sure Inventory and Printer labels are set up on the Clover dashboard.
On the KDS, tap the gear icon in the top left corner.
In Kitchen mode: tap the Printer labels you want routed to this display.
In Expo mode: tap the Printer labels you do not want routed to this display.
entries.quote: For Kitchen mode: Tap the Printer labels you would like routed to that specific display.

entries.title: Orders are not showing on the Kitchen Display
steps: Check that Inventory and Printer labels are configured on the Clover dashboard.
On the KDS tap the gear icon and check the Printer labels selected for this display.
Remember the selection works opposite ways: Kitchen mode shows the labels you tap, Expo mode hides the labels you tap.
entries.quote: For Expo mode: Tap the Printer labels you would not like routed to that specific display.

entries.title: Send online orders to a particular Kitchen Display
steps: With a single display, online orders route to the KDS automatically.
With several displays: open the Setup app on your device.
Select Online Ordering and tap the Settings tab.
Select Remote Firing Device and choose the KDS.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Select Remote Firing Device and choose your preferred KDS.

entries.title: Store a Kitchen Display
steps: Power it off with the power button on the bottom of the display.
Unplug any connected peripherals.
Keep it out of direct sunlight and high humidity.
Keep it between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
entries.quote: Power off the device by pressing the power button located on the bottom of the display.
entries.note: This article and the power-down article place the power button on the bottom; the setup article says top.

entries.title: What a Clover Kiosk needs alongside it
steps: The Kiosk requires an order printer or a Kitchen Display System to receive its orders.
It supports 100 mm VESA wall mounts.
entries.quote: Clover Kiosk supports 100 mm VESA wall mounts and requires an order printer or Kitchen Display System (KDS).

entries.title: What's in the Kiosk box
steps: Kiosk display, power cord, and a receipt paper roll.
entries.quote: Kiosk display Power cord Receipt paper roll

entries.title: First-time setup of a Clover Kiosk
steps: Connect the Kiosk to power and turn it on; it guides you through the first-time setup steps.
The system checks there are items in your account.
Give the Kiosk a device name.
Set the rollover order number and an order prefix (Clover suggests K for Kiosk).
Choose which printer Kiosk orders go to; with a Clover KDS, set ticket routing in the KDS settings.
Choose accepted order types (dine-in, takeout), customer information, order instructions, the offline payment limit, tips and special instructions.
entries.quote: Kiosk order routing: Configure which printer your Kiosk orders are sent to.

entries.title: Open Admin settings on a Kiosk
steps: Long-press the Clover logo on the bottom left of the screen.
Enter your passcode.
All Kiosk settings can be changed there at any time, or in the Setup app on the device home screen.
entries.quote: To access Admin settings, long-press on the Clover logo on the bottom left of the screen and enter your passcode.

entries.title: Kiosk order numbers and prefixes
steps: Order numbers restart at 1 when the rollover number is reached.
The order prefix is a unique character per device that shows where an order came from.
Clover recommends K for the Kiosk.
entries.quote: We recommend using unique prefixes for your devices, and using K for Kiosk.

entries.title: Kiosk payments when it goes offline
steps: A payment threshold for offline payments sets a limit for payments taken when the Kiosk loses service.
Set it in the Kiosk Admin settings.
entries.quote: Payment threshold for offline payments: Set a limit for allowing payments when the device loses service and goes offline.

entries.title: Use Kiosk Admin mode to adjust, restart or exit the Kiosk
steps: Long hold the Clover logo on the bottom left corner of the kiosk screen.
Enter the manager passcode.
From Admin mode you can change kiosk setup, open device settings, restart the kiosk, or exit the Kiosk app.
entries.quote: From here, you can make adjustments to how your kiosk is set up, access device settings, restart your kiosk, or exit the Kiosk app.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Exit Kiosk mode to reach the home screen and other apps
steps: Long hold the Clover logo on the bottom left corner of the kiosk screen.
Enter the manager passcode.
On the Admin settings screen, select Exit Kiosk mode.
You land on the kiosk home screen, where apps such as Setup and Printers are available.
entries.quote: On the Admin settings screen, select Exit Kiosk mode.

entries.title: Start the Kiosk app again
steps: Tap the Kiosk app on the home screen of the kiosk.
entries.quote: Tap the Kiosk app on the home screen of your kiosk.

entries.title: Items are not showing on the Kiosk
steps: Every item you want on the kiosk must be marked Show on Kiosk.
Turn on the Show on Kiosk toggle for the missing items.
entries.quote: All items you want to display on the kiosk must be marked as Show on Kiosk.

entries.title: Kiosk orders go to the wrong printer
steps: With several printers, the Printer Labels are probably not assigned correctly.
Assign the correct printer labels so items go to the right order printer.
entries.quote: If you have multiple printers that your kiosk routes to, it’s possible you haven’t assigned the correct Printer Labels.

entries.title: Kiosk orders are not showing on the Kitchen Display
steps: Kiosk orders reach the kitchen only when order receipts are configured correctly.
Review your order receipt setup so the kiosk routes orders to the KDS.
entries.quote: Properly configuring your order receipts is an important part of ensuring that your kiosk sends orders to your kitchen.

entries.title: Refund an order placed on the Kiosk
steps: Clover recommends refunding kiosk orders from another device or from the dashboard.
If needed, refund and void are available in the Transactions app on the kiosk.
entries.quote: To refund your kiosk orders, we recommend that you use another device or refund from the dashboard.

entries.title: Change the Kiosk 'thank you' screen message
steps: Long-press the Clover logo in the bottom left corner of the kiosk.
Enter your passcode to open Admin settings.
Select Set up your Clover Kiosk.
Scroll to Order instructions and type your message.
Select Save.
The default message is "Your order will be ready shortly."
entries.quote: The default message programmed on your kiosk is “Your order will be ready shortly.”

entries.title: Text Kiosk customers when their order is ready: setup
steps: You need a KDS or a Clover POS device (Flex, Station or Mini) to manage order statuses.
On the kiosk, long-press the Clover logo and enter your passcode.
Select Set up your Clover Kiosk and scroll to Customer information.
Tick customer phone number (and name if wanted).
Phone numbers are optional, so be ready to call out order numbers or names.
entries.quote: Select Set up your Clover Kiosk and scroll to Customer information.

entries.title: Tell a Kiosk customer the order is ready from the KDS
steps: When the order is prepared, select Complete order on the KDS (Expo or Kitchen mode).
The customer gets a text message that the order is ready for pickup.
entries.quote: in KDS Expo or Kitchen mode, select Complete order

entries.title: Tell a Kiosk customer the order is ready from the Orders app
steps: The employee needs access to view all orders in the Orders app.
Scan the barcode on the order receipt with the camera or a barcode scanner on a Station, Mini or Station Duo.
Select Mark as ready; the customer gets a text message.
Optionally tap Mark as picked up to close the order.
Without a scanner, filter Kiosk orders in the Orders app.
entries.quote: Select Mark as ready. The customer receives a text message (confirmation at the bottom of the screen).

entries.title: Let Kiosk customers pay cash at the register
steps: Long-press the Clover logo in the bottom left corner of the kiosk and enter your passcode.
At the top of the page select Payments.
Under Pay at register, tick 'Allow user to take payments at the register'.
Select Save.
Customers then see Card (Pay here) and Cash (Pay at register); cash customers get a printed receipt to take to the register.
entries.quote: Cash (Pay at register): Customer is provided a printed receipt to complete their payment at the register.

entries.title: Kiosk barcode scanner does not wake up
steps: The scanner wakes automatically when the kiosk leaves the screen-saver or welcome screen.
If it does not, tap Manual Scanner on the screen.
Make sure the kiosk is connected to an approved barcode scanner.
entries.quote: If the scanner does not activate automatically, tap Manual Scanner on the screen.

entries.title: Scanning an item on the Kiosk does nothing
steps: Scans only register when the kiosk is in active order mode.
Start an order first; scanning on other screens adds nothing and gives no feedback.
entries.quote: Scanning on non-order screens will not add items or trigger feedback.

entries.title: Kiosk scanner sounds: success chime and error tone
steps: A successful scan plays a confirmation chime, shows the item name and price, and adds the item to the cart.
A failed scan plays an error tone and shows a message explaining why.
entries.quote: Displays a message explaining why the scan failed.

entries.title: Store a Kiosk
steps: Power off the device from the device settings.
Unplug connected peripherals.
Keep it out of direct sunlight and high humidity.
Keep it between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
entries.quote: Power off the device by navigating to the device settings and selecting the power-off option.

entries.title: Item image does not appear on the Kiosk
steps: Check the item is in an active menu category enabled for Kiosk ordering and is not hidden.
Reopen the item and confirm the image shows on the Item details page.
Check the image: .jpg, .jpeg or .png, at most 10.0 MB, at least 1024 by 768px.
Check the kiosk has a working internet connection (Ethernet or Wi-Fi).
Restart or refresh the kiosk and look again.
entries.quote: Restart or refresh the kiosk and check whether the image appears.

entries.title: Image requirements for Kiosk menu items
steps: Formats: .jpg, .jpeg or .png.
Maximum size 10.0 MB.
Minimum dimension 1024 by 768px.
Very large or corrupt files may fail to upload or load.
entries.quote: Unusually large or corrupt image files may fail to upload or load on the hardware display.

entries.title: Kiosk not printing: check the paper roll
steps: Check the roll is installed correctly and has not run out.
Use thermal paper 3 1/8 inches wide by 230 feet long.
Make sure the paper is not jammed and is feeding.
entries.quote: Use thermal paper rolls measuring 3 1/8 inches wide by 230 feet long (7.0 cm x 70.1 m).
entries.note: The metric width differs between Clover articles (7.0 cm here, 7.94 cm in the paper-replacement article); 3 1/8 inches is consistent.

entries.title: Kiosk receipts faint or patchy: clean the print head
steps: Turn the device off and unplug it.
Gently clean the print head with a soft, lint-free cloth.
entries.quote: Use a soft, lint-free cloth to gently clean the print head to ensure there is no dust or debris obstructing it.

entries.title: Kiosk not printing: check Diagnostics, update and restart
steps: From the device home screen tap Diagnostics to view the printer status and queue.
Check the printer settings are set for receipt printing.
Make sure the latest update is installed.
Power the device off, wait a few minutes, and power it back on.
entries.quote: From the device home screen, tap Diagnostics.

entries.title: Print a test receipt on a Kiosk
steps: Tap the Printers app.
Select your printer.
Tap Print test receipt.
entries.quote: On your Clover device, tap the Printers app.

entries.title: Replace the paper roll in a Kiosk
steps: Use thermal paper 3 1/8 inches wide by 230 feet long.
Press the button on the right side of the kiosk to release the terminal.
Slide the terminal out to reach the printer.
Remove the empty roll.
Insert the new roll with the paper coming off the top, feeding under and through the back of the printer.
Close the printer until it clicks.
Tap Print a test receipt on the screen.
entries.quote: Open the printer by pressing the button on the right side of the kiosk to release the terminal.

entries.title: No video signal detected
steps: This Kiosk message means the display cable needs reconnecting.
Turn off the kiosk.
Remove the screws from the back support frame with a Phillips-head screwdriver.
Carefully lift the screen slightly and pull it forward.
Disconnect the display cable and reconnect it securely.
Put the screen back, refit the screws, and turn the kiosk on.
If the message comes back, contact support.
entries.quote: If your Clover Kiosk screen shows a ‘No video signal detected’ message, disconnect the display cable and reconnect the kiosk.
entries.note: Clover presents this as a merchant step even though it involves removing frame screws; escalate if the merchant is not comfortable.

entries.title: Why a Kiosk shows 'No video signal detected'
steps: It is typically caused by a loose internal display cable inside the back support frame.
Reconnecting the display cable restores the screen.
If it appears again, contact support.
entries.quote: This issue is typically caused by a loose internal display cable link inside the back support frame.

entries.title: Kiosk does not turn on or the screen stays black
steps: Check the power cord is connected to the kiosk and to the outlet.
Make sure the power switch on the back of the kiosk is turned on.
Unplug the power cord and plug it back in.
Test the outlet with another device, or plug the kiosk into a different outlet.
If it still does not turn on, contact support.
entries.quote: Make sure the power switch on the back of the kiosk is turned on.

entries.title: Kiosk still dead after checking cord, switch and outlet
steps: Contact support.
entries.quote: If the kiosk still does not turn on after trying these steps, contact Clover support.

entries.title: Clear a paper jam in a Kiosk printer
steps: Press the button on the right side of the kiosk base and pull the drawer out to reach the printer.
Press the green lever to open the print head.
Remove any jammed or damaged paper.
Close the print head and the drawer.
If it still does not print, contact support.
entries.quote: Press the green lever to open the print head.

entries.title: Kiosk not printing: fit a new paper roll (troubleshooting guide steps)
steps: Press the button on the right side of the kiosk base.
Pull the drawer out to reach the printer.
Press the green lever to open the print head.
Remove the used roll and insert a new one.
Pull a few inches of paper through and close the print head.
Close the drawer.
entries.quote: Pull a few inches of paper through and close the print head.

entries.title: Kiosk screen is unresponsive, frozen or not displaying properly
steps: Make sure the kiosk is connected to power.
Reboot the kiosk (you may need an admin passcode to exit Kiosk mode).
If it will not restart, do a hard reboot: use the power button on the back of the kiosk to power off, wait about 10 seconds, then power on again.
If it does not turn on or the screen stays unresponsive, contact support.
entries.quote: Locate the power button on the back of the kiosk, power off, wait about 10 seconds, then power on again to turn the kiosk back on.

entries.title: Kiosk screen still unresponsive after a hard reboot
steps: Contact support.
entries.quote: If the kiosk does not turn on or the screen remains unresponsive, contact Clover support.

entries.title: Item barcode will not scan at the Kiosk: add it by search
steps: Tap Search on the kiosk menu screen.
Enter the item name or product number.
Tap the item to add it to the cart.
entries.quote: Enter the item name or product number to locate the item in inventory.

entries.title: An item keeps failing to scan at the Kiosk
steps: Confirm the complete product code was saved in your inventory.
Make sure the item is set to Show on Kiosk.
Give recent inventory edits a few moments to sync to the kiosk.
entries.quote: Confirm that the complete product code was saved in your inventory.

entries.title: USB barcode scanner not scanning or not powering on
steps: Confirm the scanner is firmly connected to the USB port and getting power; use the original Clover cable hub when possible.
Try a different USB port on the cable hub.
Restart the Clover device.
Scan a barcode; the scanner should beep when it reads.
If it powers on but does not read barcodes, reset the scanner following the manufacturer instructions.
If it does not respond or communicate with the Clover device, contact support.
entries.quote: Connect the scanner to a different USB port on the cable hub.

entries.title: Scanner beeps but items do not appear
steps: Hold the scanner at the correct distance from the barcode.
Try a hard reboot of the Clover device.
Test the barcode with the built-in scanner, if the device has one.
entries.quote: Make sure the scanner is positioned at the correct distance from the barcode.

entries.title: Restart a Flex or Flex Pocket that still responds
steps: Press and hold the Power button on the right side for 2 to 3 seconds.
Tap Power off on the screen.
After the screen goes off, press and hold the Power button for 3 to 5 seconds until the Clover logo appears.
entries.quote: After the screen turns off, press and hold the Power button for 3–5 seconds until the Clover logo appears.

entries.title: Flex or Flex Pocket frozen, or card reader and scanner not working: hard reboot
steps: Connect the device to power.
Tap the screen to see if it wakes (Wake on Touch only works when connected to power).
If no battery icon shows, unplug and reconnect the power cable.
Press and hold the Power button for 40 seconds, then release.
If still unresponsive, press and hold the Power button for up to 2 minutes.
Disconnect and reconnect power and confirm the battery icon appears.
Press and hold the Power button for 3 to 5 seconds until the Clover logo appears.
If it will not turn on, reboot or charge after this, contact support.
entries.quote: Press and hold the Power button for 40 seconds, then release it.
entries.note: Clover's other hard-reboot article says hold for 32 seconds; the charging article says about 30 seconds. All three are Clover's own.

entries.title: Does a hard reboot delete anything on a Flex?
steps: No. A hard reboot restarts the device and reloads the operating system without deleting any data.
Let the battery reach at least 20% first if the charging icon appears.
entries.quote: a hard reboot resolves it without deleting any data

entries.title: Flex screen does not wake when tapped
steps: Wake on Touch only works while the device is connected to power.
Connect it to power and tap the screen again.
entries.quote: The device must be connected to power for Wake on Touch to work.

entries.title: Flex will not turn on, reboot or charge after a hard reboot
steps: Contact support.
entries.quote: If your device does not turn on, reboot, or charge after a hard reboot, contact Clover support.

entries.title: Flex or Flex Pocket does not charge, stay on, or hold a charge (troubleshooting guide)
steps: Make sure the power adapter is in a working outlet.
Connect the device to the adapter or cradle and look for a battery icon or charging light.
If it seems unresponsive, press and hold the Power button for about 30 seconds.
If still nothing, press and hold the Power button for up to one minute to restart it.
With a cradle: remove the device, unplug the cradle, wait 30 to 60 seconds, plug it back in and put the device back.
If the cradle still does not charge it, connect a USB-C cable directly to the device port.
If the battery was very low, charge for at least 30 minutes before turning it on.
If it still fails, contact support.
entries.quote: If you are using a charging cradle, remove the device, unplug the cradle, wait 30–60 seconds, then plug it back in and reconnect the device.

entries.title: Usual causes of a Flex that will not charge
steps: An outlet with no power, an unresponsive charging cradle, or a deeply drained battery.
A cradle left connected for long periods may stop transferring power; resetting it can restore charging.
entries.quote: The charging cradle may stop transferring power if it remains connected for long periods.

entries.title: Flex or Flex Pocket barcode scanner does not scan
steps: Press and hold the scanner button on the left side of the device for a few seconds.
Check the scanner or camera window is clean and undamaged.
Open the Camera app and confirm it shows an image.
Clear the cache for the Camera app.
Swipe down twice from the top of the screen, select Settings, and check for a system update.
Restart the device.
If it still does not work, contact support before going further.
entries.quote: Inspect the scanner or camera window and make sure it is clean and not damaged.

entries.title: Flex barcode scanner still not working after restart
steps: Clover's guide lists a factory reset of the device as the last step.
A factory reset erases the device, so get support on the line first.
If the scanner still does not work afterwards, the device needs support.
entries.quote: If the scanner still does not work, perform a factory reset of the device.
entries.note: Clover's factory-reset article says not to factory reset unless directed by support.

entries.title: Flex scanner reads the whole barcode only
steps: The scanner reads the entire barcode.
It cannot be set to scan only part of a barcode.
entries.quote: The barcode scanner reads the entire barcode, and you cannot customize it to scan only a partial section.

entries.title: Open device settings on a Flex
steps: Swipe down twice from the top of the screen.
Select Settings.
entries.quote: To access device settings, swipe down twice from the top of the screen and select Settings.

entries.title: Flex printer does not print or shows a printer error
steps: Make sure the battery has at least 10% charge.
Open the printer door and remove any damaged paper.
Close the printer door completely.
Open the Printers app, tap Receipt Printer, then Print Test Receipt.
If it still does not work, contact support.
entries.quote: Make sure the Flex battery has at least 10% charge.

entries.title: Usual causes of a Flex printer error
steps: A low battery, a printer door that is not latched, or a paper jam.
entries.quote: This issue is typically caused by a low battery charge, an unlatched printer door, or a rolled paper jam.

entries.title: Clear a paper jam in a Flex
steps: Make sure the Flex has at least 10% battery.
Remove any protective sleeve from the device.
Open the printer door on the back.
Remove any torn or stuck paper.
Pull the paper through the exit slot past the cutter.
Close the printer door.
Print a test receipt.
If it still jams or will not print, contact support.
entries.quote: Pull the paper through the exit slot past the cutter.

entries.title: Protective sleeve can cause Flex paper jams
steps: Jams are typically caused by torn paper fragments, a misaligned roll, or a protective sleeve blocking the printer door.
Take the sleeve off when clearing a jam.
entries.quote: This issue is typically caused by torn paper fragments, a misaligned paper roll, or a protective sleeve blocking the printer door.

entries.title: Receipt printer stops feeding or shows a paper jam
steps: Turn off the Clover device and let the printer cool if it was just used.
Open the printer lid completely.
Gently remove jammed or torn paper and every scrap inside the compartment.
Check the paper path is clear.
Reload the paper so it feeds from the back of the roll and out through the clamp.
Close the lid firmly until it clicks.
Turn the device on.
Open the Printers app, select the printer and tap Test Printer.
If jams continue, contact support.
entries.quote: Reload the receipt paper so it feeds from the back of the roll and out through the clamp.

entries.title: Prevent receipt paper jams
steps: Use only thermal receipt paper recommended for Clover devices.
Seat the roll evenly before closing the lid.
Do not overfill the printer with paper.
Never pull paper forcefully while the lid is closed.
entries.quote: Do not pull paper forcefully while the printer lid is closed.

entries.title: Receipts print blank or faint
steps: Make sure you are using thermal receipt paper.
Check the paper direction: it should feed from the bottom of the roll toward the printer head.
To find the thermal side, scratch both sides of the paper; the thermal side shows a mark.
Close the printer lid firmly until it clicks.
Open the Printers app, select your printer, then Test Printer.
If the text is faded, clean the printer heating element.
If receipts are still blank, contact support.
entries.quote: To confirm the correct side, scratch both sides of the paper. The thermal side will show a mark.

entries.title: Why receipts come out blank
steps: The roll is in the wrong way round, the paper is not thermal paper, or the printer cover is not latched.
entries.quote: Incorrect paper roll orientation, non-thermal paper rolls, or an unlatched printer cover typically cause this issue.

entries.title: Receipts print poorly or are hard to read: clean the heating element
steps: Turn off the device and let it cool for at least 2 minutes after printing.
Open the printer door and remove the paper roll.
Find the heating element near the tear bar.
Gently wipe it with a cotton swab lightly dampened with isopropyl or ethyl alcohol (90% or higher).
Do not use sharp or metal objects.
Let it dry completely.
Reload the paper and turn the device on.
If print quality does not improve, contact support.
entries.quote: Using a cotton swab lightly dampened with alcohol, gently wipe the heating element.

entries.title: Kitchen printer jams, prints unreadable or misaligned text, or has ribbon trouble
steps: Do not pull paper forcefully while the cover is closed.
Open the printer cover with the model's latch or lever.
Remove jammed or misaligned paper.
Reload the roll so it feeds straight through the tray.
If the printer uses a ribbon, remove and reseat or replace the ribbon cartridge.
Close the cover until it clicks.
Run a test receipt from the Printers app.
If problems continue, contact support.
entries.quote: If your printer uses a ribbon, remove and reseat or replace the ribbon cartridge.

entries.title: KDS bump bar does not respond or connect
steps: Check the small green power LED on the bump bar is on.
Confirm the KDS is not in sleep mode.
Press the Bump button, then another key, and see if the KDS responds.
If not, unplug the USB cable from the KDS.
Wait a few seconds, plug it back in, and listen for a connection beep.
Press Bump and another key again to confirm.
If it still does not respond, contact support.
entries.quote: Wait a few seconds, then plug the USB cable back in and listen for a connection beep.

entries.title: Third-party bump bars may not work with the Clover KDS
steps: The bump bar should be purchased from Clover or Fiserv to work properly with the KDS.
Third-party bump bars may not function correctly.
entries.quote: Third-party bump bars may not function correctly due to compatibility limitations.

entries.title: Usual causes of a dead bump bar
steps: A loose USB cable, the KDS screen being asleep, or an incompatible third-party bump bar.
entries.quote: This issue is typically caused by a loose USB cable connection, an inactive screen due to sleep mode, or an incompatible third-party accessory.

entries.title: Kitchen Display will not turn on or does not respond to touch
steps: Make sure the KDS is on a working outlet; test the outlet with another device.
Check every power cable is firmly connected to the power adapter and the back of the KDS.
Press and hold the Power button on the bottom edge of the device for 5 to 10 seconds.
Wait for the Clover logo to confirm it is turning on.
If it does not power on, contact support.
entries.quote: Press and hold the Power button on the bottom edge of the device for 5–10 seconds.

entries.title: Kitchen Display has power but will not turn on or respond
steps: The device may need to be replaced.
Contact support.
entries.quote: If the KDS receives power but does not turn on or respond, the device may need to be replaced.

entries.title: Usual causes of a dead Kitchen Display
steps: A loose power cord, a wall outlet with no power, or an internal hardware failure.
Also make sure any connected bump bar is compatible with the Clover KDS.
entries.quote: This issue is typically caused by a loose power cord, an unpowered wall outlet, or an internal hardware failure.

entries.title: Compact keeps printing receipts and will not stop
steps: Check whether several receipts or print jobs are queued on the device.
Restart the device to stop the printing.
Confirm no unprocessed transactions or print queues remain.
If it keeps printing after the restart, contact support.
entries.quote: If your Clover Compact keeps printing receipts and will not stop printing, restart the device.

entries.title: Compact frozen, stuck on a loading screen, or not responding
steps: The Compact has no power button.
Unplug the power adapter from the bottom of the device.
Wait about 10 seconds for it to power off fully.
Plug the power adapter back in.
Wait for it to power on and check it works normally.
If it does not restart or keeps freezing, contact support.
entries.quote: Unplug the power adapter from the bottom of the device.

entries.title: The Compact has no power button
steps: The Compact does not have a power button.
The Power off option on screen restarts the device rather than fully turning it off.
A hard reboot (unplug, wait, plug in) does not delete stored data.
entries.quote: The Clover Compact does not have a power button. A hard reboot clears temporary system issues but does not delete stored data.

entries.title: Compact does not turn on
steps: Check the outlet works by plugging in another device or appliance.
If the outlet works, restart the device.
Make sure the power cord is firmly connected to the Compact and plugged into a working outlet.
If it still does not power on, contact support.
entries.quote: Make sure the power cord is securely connected to the Compact and then plug it into a working power outlet.

entries.title: Compact comes back on after choosing 'Power off'
steps: This is expected: on the Compact the Power off option restarts the device instead of fully turning it off.
entries.quote: The Power off option restarts the device instead of fully turning it off.

entries.title: Compact is not printing or shows a printer error
steps: Remove and reinstall the paper roll; use thermal paper loaded in the correct direction.
Confirm the roll is the correct size for the device.
Open Settings and select Printers.
Check the printer status for error messages.
Select the printer and select Print Test Receipt.
Unplug the device and plug it back in to restart it.
Go back to Printers and print another test receipt.
If printing still does not work, contact support.
entries.quote: Unplug the device, then plug it back in to restart it.

entries.title: SSL Alert
steps: On a Compact this error means the device cannot connect and is caused by a device fault.
Troubleshooting cannot fix it.
The Compact has to be replaced; contact support.
entries.quote: This error is caused by a device issue and cannot be fixed with troubleshooting.

entries.title: Mini 3 frozen, stuck on a screen, or card reader not working: hard reboot
steps: Press and hold the power button on the left side of the screen for about 10 seconds to turn the device off.
Wait 10 to 15 seconds for it to shut down fully.
Unplug all cables, then press and hold the power button for 10 seconds to drain the battery.
Reconnect all cables.
Press and hold the power button for about 5 seconds to turn it back on.
If it does not restart or the problem continues, contact support.
entries.quote: Unplug all cables, then press and hold the power button for 10 seconds to drain the battery.
entries.note: Clover's other hard-reboot article gives one procedure for 'Mini (Gen 2 & 3)' using the green reset button behind the paper roll.

entries.title: Mini 2 (older model) frozen: hard reboot
steps: Disconnect the power adapter from the cable hub.
Open the printer compartment, remove the receipt paper, and slide the tray forward.
Press and hold the green power button for 20 seconds.
Reconnect the power cable to the hub.
Wait for the device to turn on and reconnect to the network.
entries.quote: Press and hold the green power button for 20 seconds to clear the device memory.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mini 2; the other Clover article says 15 seconds.

entries.title: Does a hard reboot delete anything on a Mini?
steps: No. It clears the device memory and reloads the operating system; it does not delete stored data.
entries.quote: A hard reboot clears the device memory and reloads the operating system. It does not delete stored data.

entries.title: Mini overheats or shuts down unexpectedly
steps: Move the Mini away from direct sunlight and heat sources, to a well-ventilated spot.
If it is stuck in a software loop, turn it off.
Let it cool down completely.
Turn it back on once cool.
entries.quote: Move the Clover Mini away from direct sunlight or heat sources.

entries.title: Mini keeps overheating or shutting down
steps: Contact support; the device may need replacement.
entries.quote: If the Clover Mini continues to overheat or shut down, contact Clover support. The device may need replacement.

entries.title: Mini does not turn on, flickers, or has power problems
steps: Make sure the power adapter is firmly connected to the power cord (some adapters have a green LED showing the outlet has power).
Check the outlet with another device, or move the Mini to a different outlet.
Make sure the power adapter is connected to the cable hub.
Check the connection from the cable hub to the bottom of the Mini.
If everything is secure, do a hard reboot.
If the Clover logo appears, reconnect any peripherals that were attached.
If it still does not turn on or keeps shutting down, contact support.
entries.quote: Check the connection from the cable hub to the bottom of the Clover Mini.

entries.title: Mini turns off when unplugged
steps: That is expected: the backup battery does not keep the Mini on when unplugged.
Keep the Mini plugged in for at least 30 minutes to charge the backup battery.
entries.quote: The backup battery does not keep the device on when unplugged.

entries.title: Mini still will not turn on after checking cables and a hard reboot
steps: Contact support; the device may need service or replacement.
entries.quote: The device may need service or replacement.

entries.title: Mini fails to print or shows printer errors
steps: Use thermal paper of the correct size and make sure the printer lid is fully closed.
Open the Printers app and check for error messages.
Select Print Test Receipt.
Restart the device with a hard reboot.
Open the Diagnostics app and select Print Queue.
Select Retry Print Jobs to print pending receipts.
If needed, select Clear Queue and reprint receipts from the Transactions app.
If the printer still does not work, contact support.
entries.quote: Select Retry Print Jobs to attempt to print any pending receipts.

entries.title: Clear stuck print jobs on a Mini
steps: Open the Diagnostics app.
Select Print Queue.
Select Retry Print Jobs, or Clear Queue.
After clearing, reprint receipts from the Transactions app.
entries.quote: If needed, select Clear Queue and manually reprint receipts from the Transactions app.

entries.title: Station Duo Gen 2 will not turn on, powers off, or shows a blank screen
steps: Make sure the power adapter is firmly connected to the power cable and a working outlet (some adapters have a green LED when powered).
Confirm the adapter is connected to the cable hub and the hub to the Station base.
Check the outlet with another device, or try a different outlet.
Press and hold the Power button on the bottom edge of the Station for 15 to 20 seconds until the Clover logo appears.
If you have them, try a different set of power cables or a different cable hub.
If it still will not power on, contact support.
entries.quote: Press and hold the Power button on the bottom edge of the Station for 15–20 seconds until the Clover logo appears.

entries.title: Station Duo Gen 2 still fails to power on
steps: The hardware or cables may need to be replaced.
Contact support.
entries.quote: If the device continues to fail to power on, the hardware or cables may need to be replaced.

entries.title: Station Duo frozen, unresponsive, or stuck on a screen (troubleshooting guide)
steps: Press and hold the power button on the customer-facing display (Mini) for about 15 seconds.
Wait for the device to turn off and start again.
If the power button does not respond, unplug the power cable from the outlet.
Wait about 15 seconds and plug it back in.
Wait for the Clover logo.
If it does not restart, contact support.
entries.quote: 1. Press and hold the power button on the customer-facing display (Mini) for about 15 seconds.
entries.note: Clover's other hard-reboot article says to unplug the display cord from the bottom of the Station for 10 seconds.

entries.title: Station Duo does not power on, screen dark, or not responding
steps: Make sure the power adapter is in a working outlet; test the outlet with another device.
Disconnect and reconnect every cable between the device base, cable hub and power adapter.
If it has power but the screen is dark, restart it: unplug the power cord from the outlet.
Wait 5 to 10 seconds, then press and hold the power button on the Mini.
Plug the power cord back in and wait for it to power on.
If it still does not turn on, contact support.
entries.quote: Wait 5 to 10 seconds, then press and hold the power button on the Mini.

entries.title: Station Duo display shows no video signal
steps: Make sure the customer-facing Mini is powered on and properly connected.
entries.quote: If the display does not show a video signal, make sure the Mini is powered on and properly connected.

entries.title: Station Duo printer gets too hot or stops working
steps: A printer that feels warm in use can be normal.
Make sure the printer cable is firmly connected to the Station Duo base; unplug it and plug it back in.
Turn the Station Duo off, then on again.
See whether the printer still overheats.
entries.quote: 2. Unplug the printer cable and plug it back in to ensure a secure connection.

entries.title: Smoke or a burning smell from the Station Duo printer
steps: Turn the device off and let it cool.
If the printer keeps overheating, stop using it and contact support.
entries.quote: If the printer continues to overheat, stop using it and contact Clover support.

entries.title: Restart a Station Solo that is on
steps: Press and hold the Power button under the screen for 2 to 3 seconds.
Select Power off.
Press and hold the Power button again for 3 to 5 seconds to turn it back on.
entries.quote: 1. Press and hold the Power button under the screen for 2–3 seconds.

entries.title: Station Solo not responding: hard reboot (troubleshooting guide)
steps: Make sure it is plugged into a working outlet.
Press and hold the Power button for 15 to 20 seconds.
Wait for it to turn off and restart; the Clover logo appears.
A hard reboot does not delete stored data.
If it does not restart, contact support.
entries.quote: 2. Press and hold the Power button for 15–20 seconds.
entries.note: Clover's other hard-reboot article says to unplug the display cord for 10 seconds.

entries.title: No light on the Station Solo power adapter
steps: That is normal: Station Solo power adapters have no indicator light.
entries.quote: Station Solo power adapters do not include an indicator light to show power status.

entries.title: Station Solo screen blank, frozen, unresponsive or displaying incorrectly
steps: Check all cable connections under the tablet stand are secure.
If the screen is off, press and hold the Power button for about 5 seconds.
If it is unresponsive, press and hold the Power button for 15 to 20 seconds to force a restart.
If the problem continues, unplug the power cord from the outlet.
Wait 15 seconds and plug it back in.
If the screen is still unresponsive, contact support.
entries.quote: Check that all cable connections under the tablet stand are securely connected.

entries.title: Station Solo will not turn on, powers off, or shows a dark screen
steps: Make sure the power adapter is in a working outlet; test with another device or try another outlet.
Check the power adapter cable is firmly connected to the cable hub.
Make sure the cable hub is firmly connected to the Station Solo base.
If all is secure, do a hard reboot.
If you have them, try another power cable or cable hub.
If it still does not turn on, contact support.
entries.quote: Make sure the cable hub is securely connected to the Station Solo base.

entries.title: Battery icon with a red slash (Station Solo)
steps: If the Station Solo shows a battery icon with a red slash, or does not power on, the device or cables may need replacing.
Contact support.
entries.quote: If the device shows a battery icon with a red slash or does not power on, the device or cables may require replacement.

entries.title: Weight scale not responding, wrong weight, or no weight in the Register app
steps: Turn off the scale and disconnect both its power cable and scale cable.
Restart the Clover device.
Reconnect the power cable first, then the scale cable.
Turn on the scale and wait until it shows 0.0.
Make sure the scale units match the item being weighed.
If the scale shows an error, calibrate it following the model instructions.
If it still does not work, contact support.
entries.quote: Reconnect the power cable first, then reconnect the scale cable.

entries.title: Activate a new Compact
steps: Peel the protective plastic film off the screen.
Plug the device in and wait for it to power on.
Choose your language.
Enter your Wi-Fi details; if Wi-Fi is unavailable, the Compact has a SIM card that can connect to a cellular network.
Enter the activation code when asked, following the on-screen instructions to retrieve it. Clover installs the latest apps.
Continue through the remaining screens.
entries.quote: Plug in your device and wait for it to power on.

entries.title: Load receipt paper in a Compact (setup article)
steps: Open the paper compartment by pulling the top of the door toward you.
Insert the roll so the end comes straight out of the slot at the top of the door.
Close the door until it clicks.
Tap on the screen to print a test receipt.
entries.quote: Open the paper compartment by grasping the top of the compartment door and pulling it toward you.

entries.title: Compact: no Wi-Fi available
steps: The Compact has a SIM card that can connect to a cellular network when Wi-Fi is unavailable.
entries.quote: If WiFi is unavailable, the Compact has a SIM card that can connect to a cellular network.

entries.title: Change the SIM card in a Compact
steps: Turn the Compact over and find the SIM card slot on the back.
Push the SIM card in to release it and pull it out.
Insert the replacement SIM and push firmly to lock it in.
entries.quote: Push the SIM card in to release it and pull it out.

entries.title: Take a payment on a Compact
steps: Tap New Sale.
Enter the sale amount.
Select a payment method.
Select an optional tip.
Swipe, tap, or insert the card.
entries.quote: To take a payment on a Clover Compact, follow the steps below:

entries.title: Authorize a card on a Compact
steps: Tap Authorization.
Tap New authorization.
Enter the authorization amount.
Insert, tap, or swipe the card.
Optionally enter a name and choose whether to give a receipt.
Availability may vary by processor.
entries.quote: To authorize a new card, tap New authorization.

entries.title: Store a Compact
steps: Power off: swipe down from the top right of the home screen (near the clock) and use the power button that appears.
Unplug all cables, including the power adapter and peripherals.
Keep it out of direct sunlight and high humidity.
Keep it between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
entries.quote: Disconnect cables by unplugging all cables, including the power adapter and any peripheral devices.

entries.title: Compact won't turn on (help article steps)
steps: The Compact powers on automatically when plugged in.
Plug another device, such as a phone charger or lamp, into the same outlet to confirm it works.
Make sure the power cord is firmly connected to both the Compact and the outlet.
Disconnect and reconnect the power cable, then try a different working outlet.
entries.quote: The Clover Compact powers on automatically when it’s plugged in.

entries.title: Restart a Compact
steps: Disconnect the power cable, then reconnect it.
entries.quote: To restart the Compact, disconnect the power cable, then reconnect it.

entries.title: Compact was off or restarted in the morning
steps: The Compact can stay on overnight.
It may restart overnight or turn off automatically after receiving Clover server updates.
If so, restart it the next time you use it.
entries.quote: The device may restart overnight or turn off automatically after receiving Clover server updates.

entries.title: Completely power off a Compact
steps: Disconnect it from the power outlet.
Or from the screen: swipe down from the top right (near the clock), select the power button, then Shut down.
entries.quote: To completely power off the Compact, disconnect it from the power outlet.

entries.title: Enter the passcode on a Compact
steps: Use the device's keypad to enter your passcode.
entries.quote: Use the device's keypad to enter your passcode.

entries.title: Compact not printing: check the paper
steps: Use thermal receipt paper, 2 1/4 inches x 85 feet (5.7 cm x 25.9 m).
Check it is loaded correctly and facing the right way, and has not run out.
Make sure the roll is not jammed, is feeding, and is not damaged or poor quality.
Look for dust, debris or paper jams in the printer.
entries.quote: Confirm you are using thermal receipt paper (2 1/4 inches x 85 feet / 5.7 cm x 25.9 m).

entries.title: Compact not printing: Diagnostics and update
steps: On the home screen tap Diagnostics and view the printer status and queue.
On the home screen tap Settings, then System > Check for system update, and make sure the software is up to date.
entries.quote: View printer status and queue, and take appropriate action.

entries.title: Compact not printing: restart and clean the print head
steps: Unplug the power adapter from underneath the device.
While unplugged, open the printer cover and find the print head.
Gently clean the print head with a soft, lint-free cloth and let it dry.
After 10 seconds or more, plug the power adapter back in.
From the device menu select Printers > Settings to confirm the settings, then print a test receipt.
entries.quote: Wait 10 seconds, and plug the power adapter back in.

entries.title: Why a Compact printer is not printing
steps: Possible causes: paper loaded incorrectly, a paper jam, incorrect settings, or a device issue.
If the test receipt fails: check printer status, reload paper, clean the print head, and restart.
entries.quote: This may be caused by incorrectly loaded paper, a paper jam, incorrect settings, or a device issue.

entries.title: Compact printer does not respond after troubleshooting and restarting
steps: The device may need to be replaced.
Contact support.
entries.quote: If the printer does not respond after troubleshooting and restarting, it may need to be replaced.

entries.title: Check you have thermal paper
steps: Scratch both sides of the paper with a fingernail or coin.
The thermal side shows a dark scratch mark.
entries.quote: Scratch both sides of the paper with a fingernail or coin; the thermal side will produce a dark, visible scratch mark.

entries.title: Compact receipts faded, streaked or missing lines: clean the heating element
steps: Turn the Compact off by unplugging it and let the printer cool for at least 2 minutes.
Open the printer door and remove the paper.
Find the heating element near the upper surface of the tray, next to the serrated tear bar.
Gently clean it with a cotton swab lightly dipped in ethyl or isopropyl alcohol (at least 90%). Do not soak the swab.
Remove any dust, debris or fibers.
Let the alcohol dry completely.
Close the door, reload the paper and plug the device back in.
Open the Printers app, select your printer and tap Print test receipt.
entries.quote: Locate the heating element near the upper surface of the tray, next to the tear bar (the serrated metal edge where receipts are cut).

entries.title: Compact heating element: what not to do
steps: Do not use water or other cleaning products; only high-purity alcohol (at least 90%).
Do not use sharp or abrasive objects.
Do not clean it while still hot.
Do not oversaturate the swab.
entries.quote: Do not use sharp or abrasive objects on the Compact, as they may damage the heating element.

entries.title: Wrong paper type in a Clover printer
steps: Non-thermal paper gives blank or faint prints and may stop the printer working properly.
entries.quote: Using non-thermal paper can result in blank or faint prints and may prevent the printer from working properly or cause it to fail.

entries.title: Replace the paper roll in a Compact
steps: Use thermal paper 2 1/4 inches wide x 85 feet long.
Lift the latch or press the button to open the printer cover.
Remove the empty roll.
Insert the new roll with the paper feeding from the bottom.
Feed the paper through until it is visible.
Close the cover so it snaps into place.
Tap Print a test receipt.
entries.quote: Insert the new roll with the paper feeding from the bottom.

entries.title: Set up a Clover Go card reader
steps: Set up the card reader using the Clover Go setup guide.
Download the Clover Go app to your phone or tablet.
Connect the reader wirelessly to the app to start taking payments.
entries.quote: download the Clover Go app to your phone or tablet and wirelessly connect your reader to the app to start taking payments

entries.title: Clover Go reader does not connect to the phone or tablet
steps: Charge the card reader.
Check the phone or tablet: iOS 11.0 or higher (iPhone 5s or later) or Android 6.0 or higher.
Turn on Bluetooth (4.0 / BTLE) and make sure the phone is on Wi-Fi or a cellular network.
Use a power supply rated at least 5V, 1000mA.
entries.quote: Bluetooth 4.0 (BTLE) enabled and connected to WiFi or a cellular network.

entries.title: Phones and tablets the Go reader does not work with
steps: Windows Phone, Amazon devices, and jailbroken or rooted devices are not supported.
entries.quote: Go card readers do not work with Windows Phone®, Amazon devices, or jailbroken or rooted devices.

entries.title: Clover Go G3 reader: blinking pink light
steps: The battery is critically low.
Plug the reader in and charge it for 1 to 2 hours.
entries.quote: Go G3 card reader: When the battery is critically low, a blinking pink light appears.

entries.title: Clover Go G2 reader shows no light
steps: The battery may be drained.
Fully charge the reader for 1 to 2 hours.
In a hurry, 10 minutes of charging gives about five card transactions.
entries.quote: charging the reader for 10 minutes lets you perform about five card transactions

entries.title: Clover Go G3 reader shows no lights when unplugged
steps: This is normal: the reader shows status lights only while plugged in.
On unplugging, the lights may flash briefly and then go out to save battery.
entries.quote: the reader does not display status lights when the device is unplugged

entries.title: Clover Go reader does not charge
steps: Contact support.
entries.quote: If your card reader does not charge, contact Clover support.

entries.title: Pair a Clover Go card reader with the Go app
steps: Turn on Bluetooth on your phone or tablet.
Log in to the Clover Go app.
From the More menu select Card reader.
Select Pair now and follow the on-screen steps.
You can pair before you start taking payments or during a sale.
entries.quote: Log in to the Clover Go app, and from the More menu, select Card reader.

entries.title: Pairing the Go reader with the app fails
steps: When pairing fails, the app shows a message with a customer support phone number.
Call that number for help.
entries.quote: If pairing your card reader with the Clover Go app fails, a message appears with a customer support phone number you can call for assistance.

entries.title: Clover Go card readers and surcharging
steps: Go card readers do not support surcharging, even on a surcharge-enabled account.
entries.quote: Go card readers do not support surcharging, even if your account is surcharge-enabled.

entries.title: Store a Clover Go reader
steps: Power it down by holding the power button for 5 to 10 seconds and confirm shutdown.
Unplug all cables.
Keep it out of direct sunlight and high humidity.
Keep it between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
entries.quote: Power down the device by holding the power button for 5-10 seconds and confirm shutdown.

entries.title: Change how soon the Go app logs you out when idle
steps: In the Go app, open the More menu and tap Settings.
Under Security, set Inactivity timeout: 15 minutes, 1 hour, 3 hours or 24 hours.
After a timeout you get back in with your passcode, fingerprint or face recognition.
entries.quote: Inactivity timeout: Set the amount of time a user can be inactive before you're logged out of the app.

entries.title: Go app: forced logout
steps: A forced logout happens when you tap Logout or the app is not used for seven days.
Log back in with email and password, then passcode, and set up fingerprint or face recognition again.
entries.quote: To log back into the app after a forced logout, enter your email and password, your passcode, and reset any fingerprint or facial recognition options.

entries.title: Go app: email and password aren't recognized
steps: This can happen when you have more than one account.
If you have logged in to this account before, tap Returning User and select your name.
If you are new to this account, enter the Clover account's email and password.
Or tap Access your account on the login screen and enter your email to get a password reset email.
entries.quote: If the Clover Go app doesn't recognize your email address and password, it might be because you have more than one account.

entries.title: Go app: passcode isn't recognized
steps: If you have logged in before, tap Switch User and select your name.
If you don't remember your passcode, have your manager reset it from the Web Dashboard.
entries.quote: If you don't remember your passcode, have your manager reset your passcode from the Web Dashboard.

entries.title: Go app: my session ended
steps: By default the Go app logs the user out after an hour of inactivity to protect the device from misuse.
entries.quote: the Go app logs out the user after an hour of inactivity by default

entries.title: Go app: can't see all my accounts
steps: A newly added account takes about 7 days to appear; wait a few days and try again.
If an account you have seen before is gone, log out, close the app, and log back in.
entries.quote: If you've seen the account before and it's no longer displayed, try logging out, closing the app, then logging back in.

entries.title: Clover Go doesn't recognize the barcode
steps: The full barcode number (UPC) must be saved on the item in your inventory.
Open the Inventory app and select Items.
Click the pencil icon next to the item.
Enter the barcode number in the Product Code field.
Click Save.
entries.quote: The full barcode number (UPC) must be added to the item in your inventory before the app can recognize it.

entries.title: Duplicated Transaction Detected
steps: The Go app shows this when the last four card digits and the amount match a recently completed transaction.
If it is not a duplicate, tap Proceed to continue.
To check earlier transactions first, click Cancel, then tap Menu > Orders & Transactions.
entries.quote: A Duplicated Transaction Detected message appears when the last four numbers of the card and the dollar amount of a transaction are the same as a recently completed transaction.

entries.title: Go app doesn't show my inventory changes
steps: Log out of the Go app and log back in.
If the changes still do not show, wait a few minutes and try again.
entries.quote: If you still don't see your changes, wait a few minutes and try again.

entries.title: Go app: can't issue a refund
steps: Refunds need the Access Transaction > Refund payments permission on the employee's role.
A blank screen appears if an item in the order was changed to an unsupported format such as variable price: change the item back, log out, then reopen the app and log in.
entries.quote: Refunds can only be issued by employees who have the Access Transaction > Refund payments permission assigned to their role.

entries.title: Tell which Station Duo generation you have
steps: Look for the device name under the base of the display.
The first generation says "Station Duo Display".
entries.quote: If you’re not sure which version you have, look for the device name under the base of the display.

entries.title: What's in the Station Duo 2 box
steps: 14" merchant display, 8" customer-facing terminal, receipt printer, screwdriver, connector cable, hub, power adapter, power cable, LAN Ethernet cable and 2 paper rolls.
Adhesive Velcro pads let you fix the hub under the counter.
A free PIN entry aid can be requested from Clover support.
entries.quote: Adhesive pads with Velcro let you attach the hub beneath the countertop to keep cables organized.

entries.title: Assemble a Station Duo 2
steps: Take everything out and connect all parts before plugging in.
Lay the display, customer-facing screen and printer upside down next to each other.
With the screwdriver, attach one end of the connector cable to the main display and the other end to the customer-facing terminal; tighten the screws by hand.
Unwind the printer cable from the printer base and connect it to the base of the display.
Connect the hub to the base of the main display.
Plug the power adapter into the hub and attach the power cord to the adapter.
Plug the power cord into a grounded outlet.
Turn each piece right side up; they power on automatically.
entries.quote: Turn each piece right side up, and they’ll power on automatically.

entries.title: Activate a Station Duo 2
steps: Have your internet ready; Clover recommends Ethernet. Wi-Fi must use WPA or WPA2 and be password-protected.
Choose your language on the display.
With the Ethernet cable plugged in, it connects automatically. For Wi-Fi, enter your Wi-Fi details and disconnect the Ethernet cable.
Enter the device activation code when asked, following the on-screen instructions to retrieve it. Clover installs the latest apps.
Continue through the remaining screens.
entries.quote: If the Ethernet cable is plugged in, you’ll automatically connect to the internet that way.

entries.title: Load paper in the Station Duo printer for the first time
steps: Open the top of the printer and press the green latch to release the printer head.
On the display, tap Continue.
Put in the thermal paper with the edge of the roll following the inside top of the compartment and out of the slot.
Close the printer door until it clicks.
entries.quote: Install the thermal paper with the edge of the roll following the inside top of the compartment and out of the slot.

entries.title: Station Duo 2 and the cash drawer
steps: The Station Duo 2 processes cash and checks with the included cash drawer.
entries.quote: Process cash and checks with the included cash drawer.

entries.title: PIN entry aid and PIN shield on a Station Duo
steps: The PIN entry aid sits on top of the customer-facing screen; its raised keys help visually impaired customers enter a PIN.
The PIN Shield sits on top of the customer-facing screen for privacy.
Request a free PIN entry aid from Clover support.
entries.quote: The raised keys make it easier for visually impaired customers to enter a PIN.

entries.title: Station Duo (1st generation) has no power buttons
steps: Once connected to power, the terminal powers on first and then the merchant display.
There are no power buttons, but there is a reset button on the reverse side of the customer-facing terminal screen.
entries.quote: There are no power buttons, but there is a reset button on the reverse side of the customer-facing terminal screen.
entries.note: First-generation Station Duo only.

entries.title: Internet options when activating a Station Duo (1st generation)
steps: Ethernet with the supplied cable, the SIM card for cellular data, or your Wi-Fi network.
If you offer Wi-Fi to customers, give them a different network.
entries.quote: Your device's SIM card can connect to cellular data service.
entries.note: First-generation Station Duo only.

entries.title: Station Duo (1st generation): which way round the main connector cable goes
steps: The main connector cable has two small screws at each end and a green arrow on one end.
The end with the green arrow goes to the base of the display; the other end goes to the base of the terminal.
Tighten screws hand-tight only.
entries.quote: Use the supplied screwdriver to connect the end of the cable with the green arrow to the base of the display, as shown.
entries.note: First-generation Station Duo only.

entries.title: Accessories and peripherals that work with a Station Duo
steps: Accessories: cash drawer, extra bill and coin tray, locking lid with 2 keys, Clover Mini PIN shield.
Peripherals: Star Micronics SP742M kitchen printer, Zebra DS2208 handheld scanner, Zebra DS9208 hands-free scanner, CAS SW-RS weight scale.
entries.quote: Star Micronics kitchen printer, model SP742M

entries.title: Use the PIN entry aid on a Station Duo
steps: Keep the aid near the terminal.
When ringing up the customer, place the aid over the terminal.
Let the customer enter the PIN.
Remove the aid and complete the sale.
entries.quote: When you ring up the customer, place the aid over the terminal. Allow the customer to enter a PIN. Remove the aid, and then complete the sale.

entries.title: Find the Station Duo serial numbers
steps: Display: starts with S053; see the label on the display base, or open Account & Setup > Devices on screen.
Customer-facing terminal: starts with C053; see the label on the terminal base.
Printer: starts with P050 or P051; see the base of the printer.
Support will ask for the customer-facing terminal serial number.
entries.quote: If you have a problem with the device and need to contact Clover support, you’ll need the customer-facing terminal serial number.

entries.title: What's in the Station Solo box
steps: Station touchscreen device, power adapter, power cable and Quick Start Guide.
The receipt printer is an optional accessory and may ship in a separate box.
entries.quote: Receipt printers are optional accessories and may ship in a separate box.

entries.title: Connect power to a Station Solo
steps: Connect the power cable to the port on the back of the device.
Connect the other end to the power adapter.
Plug the adapter cable into the power adapter.
Plug into a grounded AC outlet.
entries.quote: Connect the power cable to the port on the back of the Clover Solo device.

entries.title: Activate a Station Solo
steps: Have your internet ready; Clover recommends Ethernet. Wi-Fi must use WPA or WPA2 and be password-protected.
Choose your language.
With the Ethernet cable plugged in, it connects automatically. For Wi-Fi, enter your Wi-Fi details and disconnect the Ethernet cable.
Enter the device activation code when asked. Clover installs the latest apps.
Continue through the remaining screens.
entries.quote: If you want to connect using WiFI, enter your WiFi network information and disconnect the Ethernet cable if applicable.

entries.title: Load paper in the Station Solo printer for the first time
steps: Open the top of the printer and the green latch to release the printer head.
On the display, tap Continue.
Put in the thermal paper with the edge of the roll following the inside top of the compartment and out of the slot.
Close the printer door until it clicks.
entries.quote: Open the top of the printer and the green latch to release the printer head.

entries.title: Store a Station Duo
steps: Where possible leave it on and connected to power.
If it must be stored: connect to power, let it turn on, and wait until the battery gauge reads 100%.
Press and hold the green power button on the body of the smaller unit, under the LCD panel, until Power Off appears.
Tap Power Off and confirm.
Let it turn off completely before removing the power cable.
Store out of sunlight and humidity, between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
Recharge it every 12 months.
entries.quote: Locate the green power button on the body of the smaller unit, under the LCD panel:

entries.title: A Station Duo left unpowered too long can go into tamper mode
steps: The device has 2 batteries that keep tamper detection powered.
If the main battery fully discharges, the backup battery keeps it going for a while longer.
After that, the device's ability to process transactions may be affected.
Recharge a stored Station Duo every 12 months to avoid this.
If it has already happened, contact support.
entries.quote: For long-term storage that does not trigger tamper detection, recharge your Station Duo (serial numbers starting with C053, C153, or S053) every 12 months.

entries.title: Store a Station Solo
steps: Where possible leave it on and connected to power.
If it must be stored: connect to power, let it turn on, and wait until the battery gauge reads 100%.
Press and hold the white power button on the bottom edge of the display, right-hand side, until Power Off appears.
Tap Power Off and confirm.
Let it turn off completely before removing the power cable.
Store out of sunlight and humidity, between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
Recharge it at least every 12 months.
entries.quote: Locate the white power button on the bottom edge of the display, on the right-hand side.

entries.title: A Station Solo left unpowered too long can go into tamper mode
steps: The device has 2 batteries that keep tamper detection powered.
Recharge a stored Station Solo at least every 12 months so tamper detection is not triggered.
If both batteries run flat, the device's ability to process transactions may be affected; contact support.
entries.quote: For long-term storage that does not trigger tamper detection, recharge your Station Solo (serial number starting with C051) at least every 12 months.

entries.title: Station printer not printing: check the paper roll
steps: Check the roll is installed correctly and has not run out.
Use thermal paper 3 1/8 inches wide by 230 feet long.
Make sure the paper is not jammed and is feeding.
entries.quote: Use thermal paper rolls measuring 3 1/8 inches wide by 230 feet long (7.0 cm x 70.1 m).

entries.title: Station receipts faint or patchy: clean the print head
steps: Turn the device off and unplug it.
Gently clean the print head with a soft, lint-free cloth.
entries.quote: Use a soft, lint-free cloth to gently clean the print head to ensure no dust or debris is obstructing it.

entries.title: Station printer not printing: Diagnostics, update and restart
steps: On the home screen tap Diagnostics to view the printer status and queue.
Check the printer settings in the device menu are set for receipt printing.
Make sure the latest update is installed.
Power the device off, wait a few minutes, and power it back on.
entries.quote: Navigate to the printer settings in the device’s menu to confirm or adjust them.

entries.title: Print a test receipt on a Station
steps: Tap the Printers app.
Select your printer.
Tap Print test receipt.
entries.quote: On your Clover device, tap the Printers app.

entries.title: Replace the paper roll in a Station Duo printer
steps: Use thermal paper 3 1/8 inches wide by 230 feet long.
Open the top of the printer and press the green latch to release the printer head.
Remove the empty roll.
Insert the new roll with the paper following along the top.
Close the printer door until it clicks.
Tap Print a test receipt on the display.
entries.quote: To replace the Station Duo receipt printer paper, use thermal paper rolls measuring 3 ⅛ inches wide by 230 feet long, (7.94 cm x 70.1 m).

entries.title: Replace the paper roll in a Station Solo printer
steps: Use thermal paper 3 1/8 inches wide by 230 feet long.
Open the top of the printer and press the green latch to release the printer head.
Remove the empty roll.
Insert the new roll with the paper following along the top.
Close the printer door until it clicks.
Tap Print a test receipt on the display.
entries.quote: To replace the Station Solo receipt printer paper, use thermal paper rolls measuring 3 ⅛ inches wide by 230 feet long (7.94 cm x 70.1 m).

entries.title: Tell which Mini version you have
steps: Look for the version name under the base of the display.
entries.quote: If you're not sure which Mini version you have, look for the version name under the base of the display.

entries.title: Connect the Mini hub, power and accessories
steps: Plug the power brick's circular plug into the white hub.
Plug the power cord into the power brick and the other end into a power source.
Optionally use the white USB cord to connect accessories such as the cash drawer or a scanner to the hub.
entries.quote: (Optional) Use the white USB cord to connect other accessories (such as the cash drawer, scanner, etc.) to the hub.

entries.title: Reverse the direction of the Mini hub cable
steps: Use the green screwdriver to loosen the hub connector on the underside of the device.
Reverse the cable direction.
Tighten the green screw until the screw's head is level with the charging cable.
entries.quote: Tighten the green screw until the screw's head is level with the charging cable.

entries.title: Mini doesn't power on when plugged in
steps: Leave the Mini plugged in for at least 30 minutes so the backup battery can charge.
Unplug all cables from the hub.
Press and hold the power button, in the receipt compartment at the back of the Mini, for 20 seconds.
Plug the black power cable back into the hub.
When the Clover logo shows, plug the other cables back in.
entries.quote: Leave the Mini plugged into a power source for at least 30 minutes to allow the backup battery to charge.

entries.title: Connect a Mini to the network during setup
steps: An internet connection is needed to activate the device.
Clover recommends Ethernet for countertop devices.
If the Ethernet cable is already in the hub, the Mini tries Ethernet automatically.
For Wi-Fi, enter the network name and password; the network must use WPA or WPA2 and be closed and secure.
entries.quote: If your Ethernet cable is already plugged into the hub, your device automatically tries to connect using Ethernet.

entries.title: Activate a Mini
steps: After powering on, follow the Setup Wizard.
Choose your language and make sure the device is online.
When asked for an activation code, follow the on-screen instructions to retrieve it and enter it. Clover installs the latest apps.
Continue through the remaining screens.
entries.quote: During device setup, you'll be prompted to enter an activation code.

entries.title: Find the Mini serial number
steps: On a Clover device go to Setup > Devices and look in the ID column.
Or open the receipt paper door on the back and look on the black plastic tab under the paper roll.
Serials start C030 or C031 (Mini), C032 (Mini 2nd generation), C035 (Mini 3).
entries.quote: On the back of the device, open the receipt paper door and look on the black, plastic tab under the paper roll.

entries.title: Mini serial number prefixes by model
steps: C030 or C031: Mini.
C032: Mini (2nd generation).
C035: Mini 3.
entries.quote: Mini 3 serial numbers start with C035

entries.title: Which devices a Mini can be tethered to
steps: Mini and Mini (2nd generation): to a Mini, Mini (2nd generation), Station or Station 2.
Mini 3: only to another Mini 3.
entries.quote: Mini (2nd generation): Mini, Mini (2nd generation), Station, Station 2, 3rd party

entries.title: Connect a customer-facing Mini to a merchant-facing Mini
steps: Use a USB cord with a type A plug on one end and type B on the other.
Merchant-facing device: plug the Type A end into one of the 4 USB ports on the Mini hub.
Customer-facing device: plug the Type B end into the second port on the Mini hub's left.
Install the USB Pay Display app on both devices when prompted.
Tap USB Pay Display to launch the customer-facing display; your business name appears.
entries.quote: For the customer-facing device: Plug in Type B USB to the second port on the Mini hub’s left.

entries.title: Not prompted to install the USB Pay Display app
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select More > App Market.
Search for the USB Pay Display app and connect it to your account.
It must be installed on both the merchant-facing and customer-facing devices.
entries.quote: The USB Pay Display app must be installed on both merchant-facing and customer-facing devices.

entries.title: Error message on a tethered Mini (USB Pay Display)
steps: Check the USB cable connections between the two devices.
Check that both devices have the USB Pay Display app installed.
entries.quote: Check that both devices have the USB Pay Display app installed.

entries.title: Switch a customer-facing Mini back to merchant-facing
steps: On the customer-facing Mini, tap all four corners of the touchscreen at the same time, using both hands.
Log in to the Mini.
entries.quote: On the customer-facing Mini, use both hands to tap all four corners of the touchscreen simultaneously.

entries.title: Put a Mini into customer-facing mode
steps: Tap the USB Pay Display app.
A screen showing how to exit customer-facing mode shows for a few seconds.
In customer-facing mode the Mini shows "Welcome to [Your Business Name]".
entries.quote: Tap the USB Pay Display app to launch the customer-facing Mini display.

entries.title: Store a Mini
steps: Where possible leave it on and connected to power.
If it must be stored: connect to power, let it turn on, and wait until the battery gauge reads 100%.
Open the printer door, remove the paper roll and find the green power button.
Press and hold it until Power Off appears; tap Power Off and confirm.
Let it turn off completely before removing the power cable.
Store out of sunlight and humidity, between 0°C (32°F) and 40°C (105°F).
entries.quote: When the battery gauge reads 100%, turn off the device:

entries.title: A Mini left unpowered too long can go into tamper mode
steps: The Mini has 2 batteries that keep tamper detection powered.
Recharge a stored Mini every 6 months (serials starting C030, C031) or every 12 months (C032, C035).
If both batteries run flat, the device's ability to process transactions may be affected; contact support.
entries.quote: Every 6 months: Mini devices whose serial numbers start with C030, C031.

entries.title: Replace the paper roll in a Mini
steps: Use thermal paper 2 1/4 inches wide by 85 feet long.
Open the printer door on the back of the device.
Remove the empty roll.
Insert the new roll, feeding the paper from the bottom.
Pull a little paper out so the end sticks out of the printer.
Close the cover until it clicks.
Tap Print a test receipt.
entries.quote: Insert the new roll, feeding the paper from the bottom.

entries.title: Mini not printing: check the paper roll
steps: Check the roll is installed correctly and has not run out.
Use thermal paper 2 1/4 inches wide by 85 feet long.
Make sure the paper is not jammed and is feeding.
entries.quote: Use thermal paper rolls that are 2 1/4 inches wide by 85 feet long.

entries.title: Mini receipts faint or patchy: clean the print head
steps: Turn the device off and unplug it.
Gently clean the print head with a soft, lint-free cloth.
entries.quote: Use a soft, lint-free cloth to gently clean the print head to ensure there is no dust or debris obstructing it.
